dharmakirti/nyaya-bindu/1.12-17.sanskrit_iast: tasya viṣayaḥ svalakṣaṇam. yasya arthasya saṃnidhāna-asaṃnidhānābhyāṃ jñāna-pratibhāsa-bhedas tat svalakṣaṇam. tad eva paramārthasat. arthakriyāsāmarthya-lakṣaṇatvād vastunaḥ. anyat sāmānyalakṣaṇam. so anumānasya viṣayaḥ.
dharmakirti/nyaya-bindu/1.12-17.english_close: Its object is the svalakṣaṇa. That entity whose presence and absence make the appearance of cognition differ is the svalakṣaṇa. That alone is ultimately real, because a thing is marked by capacity for causal efficacy. What is other is the sāmānyalakṣaṇa. That is the object of inference.

abhinavagupta/ishvara-pratyabhijna-vimar.sanskrit_iast: yathāruci yathārthitvaṃ yathāvyutpatti bhidyate / ābhāso 'py artha ekasminn anusaṃdhānasādhite // ... nanvevaṃ cet kathamekaṃ svalakṣaṇam ? ucyate ---- teṣāṃ pṛthak bhāsamānānāmapi ābhāsānāṃ yo vimarśaḥ anuprāṇitabhūtaḥ ... tadā tadekaṃ svalakṣaṇam
abhinavagupta/ishvara-pratyabhijna-vimar.english_close: Appearance, though one object has been established by synthesis, differs according to taste, need, and learned usage. How then is there one svalakṣaṇa? It is said: when the separately appearing manifestations are animated by reflective synthesis, then that single thing is the svalakṣaṇa.

abhinavagupta/ishvara-pratyabhijna-vimar.sanskrit_iast: sā tu deśādikādhyakṣāntarabhinne svalakṣaṇe / tātkālikī pravṛttiḥ syād arthinaḥ // ... naikaikataḥ pramāṇāt sā pravṛttiḥ api tu pramāṇasamūhādeva
abhinavagupta/ishvara-pratyabhijna-vimar.english_close: That immediate activity of the desirer takes place with respect to the svalakṣaṇa not different from the other perceptions such as place and the rest. Such activity does not arise from any single means of knowledge, but from the aggregate of means of knowledge.

sankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/2.1.14.sanskrit_iast: tadananyatvam ārambhaṇaśabdādibhyaḥ | ... kāryamākāśādikaṃ bahuprapañcaṃ jagat, kāraṇaṃ paraṃbrahma, tasmātkāraṇāt paramārthato 'nanyatvaṃ vyatirekeṇābhāvaḥ kāryasyāvagamyate ... 'vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttiketyeva satyam' ... vācārambhaṇaśabdena ca vikārajātasyānṛtatvābhidhānāt.
sankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/2.1.14.english_close: The effect-world is non-different from the supreme Brahman as cause; apart from the cause the effect has no independent reality. The modification is only a name beginning in speech, and the whole class of modifications is declared unreal.

ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/§8.sanskrit_iast: apare tv apahatapāpmatvādisamastakalyāṇaguṇopetam api brahmaitenaivāikyāvabodhena kenacid upādhiviśeṣeṇa saṃbaddhaṃ badhyate mucyate ca nānāvidhamalarūpapariṇāmāspadaṃ ceti vyavasthitāḥ.
ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/§8.english_close: Others hold that Brahman, though endowed with all auspicious qualities, is by this very cognition of identity connected with a certain limiting adjunct, becomes bound and released, and is the locus of manifold transformations of impure form.

ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/§9.sanskrit_iast: anye punar aikyāvabodhayāthātmyaṃ varṇayantaḥ svābhāvikaniratiśayāparimitodāraguṇasāgaraṃ brahmaiva ... svabhāvato vilakṣaṇam avilakṣaṇaṃ ca viyadādinānāvidhamalarūpapariṇāmāspadaṃ ceti pratyavatiṣṭhante.
ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/§9.english_close: Others again, while describing reality through cognition of identity, maintain that Brahman itself, an ocean of unsurpassed and measureless exalted qualities, is by nature both different and non-different and is the locus of manifold transformations such as space and the rest.

ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/§15.sanskrit_iast: tajjñānenāsya nikhilasya jñātatāṃ bruvaṃl lokadṛṣṭaṃ kāryakāraṇayor ananyatvaṃ darśayituṃ dṛṣṭāntam āha -- yathā somyaikena mṛtpiṇḍena sarvaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syād vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttikety eva satyam iti.
ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/§15.english_close: To show that by knowing that one all this is known, scripture gives the familiar example of non-difference of effect and cause: by one lump of clay all things made of clay are known; the modification is only a name arising in speech, while clay alone is the reality.

ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/§16.sanskrit_iast: sa hovāca sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam iti ... tasmin kāle jagataḥ sadātmakatāṃ sad eveti pratipādya ... sadāpannasya jagatas tadānīm avibhaktanāmarūpatāṃ pratipādya tatpratipādanenaiva sato jagadupādānatvaṃ pratipāditam.
ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/§16.english_close: ‘Being alone, one without a second, was this in the beginning’: this teaches that the world was of the nature of sat before creation, with name and form then undivided, and thereby establishes that sat is the material cause of the world.

ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/§18.sanskrit_iast: evaṃ samastacidacidātmakaprapañcasya sadupādānatāsannimittatāsadādhāratāsanniyamyatāsaccheṣatādi sarvaṃ ca ... aitadātmyam idaṃ sarvaṃ tatsatyam iti kṛtsnasya jagato brahmātmakatvam eva satyam iti pratipādya kṛtsnasya jagataḥ sa evātmā kṛtsnaṃ jagat tasya śarīram.
ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/§18.english_close: Thus, after teaching the whole cit-acit cosmos as having Sat as material cause, efficient cause, support, controller, and end, scripture declares that the entire world has Brahman as its self and that the entire world is his body.

annambhatta/tarka-sangraha/38.english_close: A cause is that which antecedently exists with respect to a determinate effect.

annambhatta/tarka-sangraha/39.english_close: An effect is the counterpositive of prior non-existence.

annambhatta/tarka-sangraha/40.english_close: Cause is threefold, by distinction of samavāyi, asamavāyi, and nimitta.

annambhatta/tarka-sangraha/80.sanskrit_iast: anādiḥ sāntaḥ prāgabhāvaḥ / utpatteḥ pūrvaṃ kāryasya.
annambhatta/tarka-sangraha/80.english_close: Prior non-existence is beginningless but has an end; it is the state of the effect before its production.

umasvati/tattvartha-sutra/sat-dravya-lak.english_close: The mark of real substance is this: the real is endowed with origination, decay, and permanence.

umasvati/tattvartha-sutra/guna-paryayava.english_close: Substance is that which possesses qualities and modes.

aksapada/nyaya-sutra/4.1.19.english_close: Īśvara is the cause, since one observes that human action is fruitless without him. (siddhānta-sūtra)

aksapada/nyaya-sutra/4.1.20.english_close: No, because in the absence of human action no fruit arises. (pūrvapakṣa-sūtra)

aksapada/nyaya-sutra/4.1.21.english_close: Since human action is itself caused by him, it does not constitute a counter-cause. (siddhānta-sūtra)

nagarjuna/mula-madhyamaka-karika/24.40.sanskrit_iast: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyatīdaṃ sa paśyati / duḥkhaṃ samudayaṃ caiva nirodhaṃ mārgam eva ca //
nagarjuna/mula-madhyamaka-karika/24.40.english_close: He who sees this dependent arising sees suffering, its arising, its cessation, and the path.

sankara/chandogya-upanisad-bhasya/6.3.2-.sanskrit_iast: sadātmanā satyatvābhyupagamāt / sarvaṃ ca nāmarūpādi sadātmanaiva satyaṃ vikārajātaṃ svatas tv anṛtam eva / … ataḥ sadātmanā sarvavyavahārāṇāṃ sarvavikārāṇāṃ ca satyatvaṃ sato ’nyatvenānṛtatvam iti
sankara/chandogya-upanisad-bhasya/6.3.2-.english_close: Because their truth is admitted only with Sat as their self: all name and form and the like is true only with Sat as its self; the class of modifications is untrue in itself. Therefore all transactions and all modifications are true with Sat as their self, and untrue as other than Sat.

sankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/1.1.12-dviru.sanskrit_iast: dvirūpaṃ hi brahmāvagamyate, nāmarūpavikārabhedopādhiviśiṣṭaṃ, tadviparītaṃ ca sarvopādhivivarjitam / tatrāvidyāvasthāyāṃ brahmaṇa upāsyopāsakādikṣaṇaḥ sarvo vyavahāraḥ / eka eva tu paramātmeśvaras tais tair guṇaviśeṣair viśiṣṭa upāsyo …
sankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/1.1.12-dviru.english_close: Brahman is understood in two modes: as qualified by name, form, modification, difference, and limiting adjuncts, and as the contrary, free of every limiting adjunct. In the state of ignorance, all transaction consisting in Brahman as worshipped and worshipper takes place. Yet the supreme Self, the Lord, is one and is worshipped as qualified by the various particular qualities.

sankara/gita-bhasya/7.4-maya-sakti.sanskrit_iast: itīyaṃ yathoktā prakṛtir me mamaiśvarī māyā-śaktir aṣṭadhā bhinnā bhedam āgatā
sankara/gita-bhasya/7.4-maya-sakti.english_close: This prakṛti just described is mine—my sovereign māyā-power—divided eightfold and come to differentiation.

sankara/gita-bhasya/7.14-svabhava-bhuta.sanskrit_iast: daivī devasya mameśvarasya viṣṇoḥ svabhāva-bhūtā hi yasmād eṣā yathoktā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā
sankara/gita-bhasya/7.14-svabhava-bhuta.english_close: This divine, guṇa-made māyā of mine is of the nature of the god—of me, the Lord Viṣṇu—and is difficult to cross.

sankara/gita-bhasya/9.1-vijnana.sanskrit_iast: idam eva tu samyagjñānaṃ sākṣāt mokṣaprāptisādhanam vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti, ātmaivedaṃ sarvam, ekam evādvitīyam ityādiśrutismṛtibhyaḥ … vijñānasahitam anubhavayuktam
sankara/gita-bhasya/9.1-vijnana.english_close: This alone is right knowledge, directly the means to liberation: ‘Vāsudeva is all,’ ‘this all is the Self,’ ‘one only, without a second,’ and the like. It is joined with vijñāna, that is, joined with experience.

sankara/gita-bhasya/9.4-5.sanskrit_iast: na hi nirātmakaṃ kiṃcid bhūtaṃ vyavahārāyāvakalpate / ato matsthāni mayātmanā ātmavattvena sthitāni … na cāhaṃ teṣu bhūteṣv avasthitaḥ … na hy asaṃsargi vastu kvacid ādheyabhāvenāvasthitaṃ bhavati
sankara/gita-bhasya/9.4-5.english_close: No being devoid of the Self can be available for transaction. Therefore beings are said to be in me because they stand with me as their self. Yet I do not abide in those beings: a non-connected reality cannot anywhere abide as a contained thing.

ramana/upadesa-saram/24.english_close: Of Īśa and the jīva, there is a difference of guise and cognition; with respect to their nature as Sat, reality is one alone.

madhva/anuvyakhyana/2.1.85-86.sanskrit_iast: nānyad anyatvam āpannaṃ kvacid dṛṣṭaṃ kathañcana / ato jīvasya na brahmabhāvaḥ syād dhi kadācana // kvacid bhinnatayā dṛṣṭaṃ tadabhinnatayā katham / dṛśyen no dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hi tādṛśaṃ na ca dṛśyate //
madhva/anuvyakhyana/2.1.85-86.english_close: Nothing that has acquired otherness is ever seen anywhere not to be other. Therefore the jīva can never have Brahman-nature. If something is seen as different somewhere, how could it be seen as non-different? Such a thing has not previously been seen, nor is it seen.

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/1.sanskrit_iast:
oṃ viśvaṃ viṣṇurvaṣaṭkāro bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ |
bhūtakṛdbhūtabhṛdbhāvo bhūtātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: He whose manifestation is the whole universe of forms: the virāṭ-puruṣa
The all-pervading one
The sacred vaṣaṭ call through which offerings are made
He who is the Lord (Prabhu) of the Past (bhūta), the Future (Bhavya) and the Present (Bhavat)
The Creator (kṛt) of all creatures (bhūta)
The sustainer and nourisher of all beings
Existence becoming all moving and unmoving beings
He is the ātman of all the beings: The very 'Be' in all the living beings
The creator and nourisher of all beings

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/2.sanskrit_iast:
pūtātmā paramātmā ca muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ |
avyayaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣī kṣetrajño'kṣara eva ca ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The supremely pure Self
The supreme self beyond all material limitations
He who is the final Goal, that is reached by all the liberated souls
The changeless and imperishable one
One who dwells in the Fort-city
Witness
One who knows the body and all the experiences from within the body, is the Knower-of-the-field, kṣetrajñaḥ
Indestructible

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/3.sanskrit_iast:
yogo yogavidāṃ netā pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ |
nārasiṃhavapuḥ śrīmān keśavaḥ puruṣottamaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The one who is to be known or realized through yoga
One who guides all the activities of all men 'who knows yoga' (Yogavit)
Lord of both pradhāna and puruṣa
One whose form is half human and half lion
One who is always with Śrī
He who has beautiful and graceful (Va) locks of hair (keśa) is familiar as in Lord Kṛṣṇa's form
The supreme person, beyond the perishable and imperishable

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/4.sanskrit_iast:
sarvaḥ śarvaḥ śivaḥ sthāṇurbhūtādirnidhiravyayaḥ |
sambhavo bhāvano bhartā prabhavaḥ prabhurīśvaraḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: He who is the all
The auspicious one who bestows auspiciousness
The One who is Eternally Pure
The firm and immovable one
The very cause for the five great elements: Space, Air, Fire, Water and Earth
The Imperishable treasure
One who takes up by his own free-will various incarnations for the glory of the world is saṃbhavaḥ
To do bhāvanā is to give: One who gives everything to His devotees is bhāvanaḥ
The One who 'Governs' the entire living world
The One who is the very womb of all the Five Great Elements
The Almighty Lord
The independent lord whose power needs no aid

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/5.sanskrit_iast:
svayambhūḥ śambhurādityaḥ puṣkarākṣo mahāsvanaḥ |
anādinidhano dhātā vidhātā dhāturuttamaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The one who manifests Himself from Himself is considered as self-made
He who brings Auspiciousness— both inner goodness and outer prosperity to His devotees
The golden person shining within the sun
One who has eyes like the lotus
The one whose commanding voice is thunderous
One who has neither birth (ādi) nor death (Nidhanam)
One who is the Substratum for the world of names and forms, and who supports all fields of experiences in all
The One who is the Dispenser of all 'fruits-of-actions'
The supreme essence underlying every existent thing

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/6.sanskrit_iast:
aprameyo hṛṣīkeśaḥ padmanābho'maraprabhuḥ |
viśvakarmā manustvaṣṭā sthaviṣṭhaḥ sthaviro dhruvaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The one beyond definition and comparison
The lord of the senses
One from whose navel springs the Lotus, which is the seat of the four-faced Creator
The Lord of the Immortals, the Devas
The maker of the universe and all experience
The reflective thinker who contemplates the highest
One who makes gross things of huge dimensions into minutest particles
The supremely gross—the whole universe as Viṣṇu's form
The Ancient (Sthavirah) and the Motionless or firm (Dhruvah)

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/7.sanskrit_iast:
agrāhyaḥ śāśvataḥ kṛṣṇo lohitākṣaḥ pratardanaḥ |
prabhūtastrikakubdhāma pavitraṃ maṅgalaṃ param ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The ungraspable subject, never an object of perception
That which remains at all times the same is the Permanent
The dark-hued one
Red-eyed
The supreme destroyer
The ever-full and abundant one
One who is the very foundation or support (dhāma) of the three quarters (Kakubh)
One who gives purity to the heart
Mangalam is that which not only removes the dark pains of evil, but brings the bright joys of merit

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/8.sanskrit_iast:
īśānaḥ prāṇadaḥ prāṇo jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prajāpatiḥ |
hiraṇyagarbho bhūgarbho mādhavo madhusūdanaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The Controller of all the five Great Elements
One who gives (dadāti) the prāṇas to all
The life-breath that sustains all
Older than all
The most excellent and glorious one
The Lord (Pati) of all living creatures (prajāḥ)
One who dwells in the womb (garbha) of the world (hiraṇya)
One who is the very womb of the world (bhūḥ)
The Lord of māyā, Spouse of Mahālakṣmī
One who destroyed the great demon Madhu

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/9.sanskrit_iast:
īśvaro vikramī dhanvī medhāvī vikramaḥ kramaḥ |
anuttamo durādharṣaḥ kṛtajñaḥ kṛtirātmavān ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One who is Omnipotent, and so has all powers in Him to the full
One full of prowess (Vikrama), courage, daring
The wielder of the divine bow Śārṅga
Supremely intelligent; One who is capable of understanding everything
The one of mighty stride who measured the universe
He who is All — Pervading is kramaḥ
One who is 'incomparably Great' in glory-anuttamaḥ
One who cannot be attacked, stormed or beleaguered successfully
The knower of all deeds
The One, who is the very dynamism behind all activities
One who is the Self in all beings

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/10.sanskrit_iast:
sureśaḥ śaraṇaṃ śarma viśvaretāḥ prajābhavaḥ |
ahaḥ saṃvatsaro vyālaḥ pratyayaḥ sarvadarśanaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The lord of the gods
The Refuge for all who are suffering from the thraldom of imperfection in life
One who is Himself the Infinite Bliss
The seed from which the universe arises
He from whom all living creatures (prajā) spring forth (Bhava) is known as prajābhavaḥ
Ahan has got two meanings: the 24-hour-day or the 12-hour day-time
The Lord of Time, from whom the concept of time arises
One who is unapproachable
One whose very nature is Knowledge
The all-seeing one

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/11.sanskrit_iast:
ajaḥ sarveśvaraḥ siddhaḥ siddhiḥ sarvādiracyutaḥ |
vṛṣākapirameyātmā sarvayogaviniḥsṛtaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: Unborn
God of all gods or the Supreme Controller of all
One who has achieved all that has to be achieved, as He Himself is the Final Goal for all
He who is available for recognition (Siddha) everywhere at all points in His nature as Pure Consciousness
The beginning of all
The unfallen and ever-pure one
The Boar who raises the world from adharma to dharma
One who has His manifestations (ātmā) in Infinite varieties, almost unaccountable (Ameya)
The one free from every bond and attachment

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/12.sanskrit_iast:
vasurvasumanāḥ satyaḥ samātmā'sammitaḥ samaḥ |
amoghaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣo vṛṣakarmā vṛṣākṛtiḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The One who is the very support of all elements, and the One who Himself is the very Essence of the elements
The one whose mind is supremely pure
He is the Real
He who is equally in all
The acceptable one
Equal; the same
The unfailing one whose acts are never futile
The one realized in the lotus of the heart
The one whose actions are dharma
One who is of the form (ākṛti) of dharma (vṛṣa)

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/13.sanskrit_iast:
rudro bahuśirā babhrurviśvayoniḥ śuciśravāḥ |
amṛtaḥ śāśvatasthāṇurvarāroho mahātapāḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One who makes all people weep
One who has many heads
One who rules over the worlds
One who is the Total Cause from which alone the entire world of experiences (visvam) has emerged out
One who has beautiful and efficient ears
One who is Immortal and Immutable
One who is both permanent (śāśvataḥ) and irremovable (sthāṇuḥ)
He who is the most Glorious (Vara) Destination (āroha)
One of great Tapas

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/14.sanskrit_iast:
sarvagaḥ sarvavidbhānurviṣvakseno janārdanaḥ |
vedo vedavidavyaṅgo vedāṅgo vedavit kaviḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The all-pervading one who has gone everywhere
One who is All- Knowing (Sarvavit) and Effulgent (bhānuḥ)
The one before whom hostile armies scatter
The one who brings sorrow to the vicious and joy to the good
The Veda; knowledge itself
One who knows the veda
He who has no imperfections (Vyanga) anywhere in him—The All — Perfect
One whose very limbs are the Vedas
The knower and contemplator of the Veda
The seer

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/15.sanskrit_iast:
lokādhyakṣaḥ surādhyakṣo dharmādhyakṣaḥ kṛtākṛtaḥ |
caturātmā caturvyūhaścaturdaṃṣṭraścaturbhujaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One who presides over all fields of experiences — all lokas
The lord of the gods
Presiding over the activities of the living organisms, Consciousness revels, illumining both the good and the evil therein
The one who is both cause and manifested effect
The fourfold self
One who manifests into the four mighty powers (vyūha)
The four-tusked one

anagho vijayo jetā viśvayoniḥ punarvasuḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: Self — Effulgent Consciousness illumines everything; and it is not borrowing Its Light from any other source

The "Experiencer"

The Victorious
Ever Successful

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The younger brother of Indra

One who has infinite strength and vitality

He who destroys the mighty heroes
The lord of Lakṣmī
The one sweet as honey to his devotees

One who is the Supreme Master of all māyā
The Great Enthusiast: the Ever — Dynamic Accomplisher
One who has Supreme Strength
The one of great intelligence
One who is the Supreme Essence
All — Powerful
Of Splendorous Light
One whose form is indefinable, indescribable, inexplicable
The possessor of glory
He whose Essence (ātmā) is inestimable and immeasurable (Ameya)
One who supports the great Mountain

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/20.sanskrit_iast:

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The wielder of the great bow Śārṅga

The permanent abode of Śrī

One, who is the Lord of all 'seers' and "Men of Wisdom"

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The ray of light in all that shines

One who destroys

Unborn

One who rules over the universe
The self celebrated throughout the Vedas
The destroyer of the enemies of the gods

Dynamic Truth

One who remains unwinking

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One who guides us to the end - the peak

Fire

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The one beyond all counting

One who is Pure

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The controller of actions and dispenser of their results

The one whose depths contain the source of creation

The solitary and distinct one
The ocean for all the rivers of all scriptural thoughts

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: He who has graceful arms

One who is cloquent of His Glory
One who is Lord of even Indra, the Lord of gods

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One who is the possessor (Dharah) of Perfect physical virility (Ojas), all brilliancy (Tejas) and every beauty (dyuti)
The Effulgent Self
The One who manifests Himself as the Essential Thermal Energy, that lends Life Potential to the very atmosphere around each living creature
One who is ever full of all prosperity
The one whose imperishable syllable is clear
One who is of the nature of the Mantras of the Vedas
Rays of the moon
The Effulgence of the Sun

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The source of the nectar-rayed moon

The moon marked like a hare
The lord of the shining gods
Medicine

One who fulfils all desires
One who is of enchanting form

The life manifest in every living being
One who gives strength (prāṇa) to everywhere
The Brother of Indra
The ocean, treasury of the waters
The Substratum for the entire universe
The unerring one who is never careless

The Valiant
Kṛṣṇa, descendant of Śūrasena
The Lord of the people (jana)
A hearty well-wisher, or friend of everyone

maharddhirṛddho vṛddhātmā mahākṣo garuḍadhvajaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One who has the lotus in his navel

One who is being meditated upon in the centre of the lotus-of-the-heart
One who sustains or nourishes all bodies
The one of magnificent prosperity and power

The ancient Self
The great-eyed one
One who has the eagle (Garuda) as his insignia on his flag

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: Incomparable

The formidable and awe-inspiring one

The receiver of all oblation
The one indicated by every valid mark and method of knowledge
The consort of Lakṣmī
Ever — Victorious

The Fish incarnation
The Path
The Cause

All enduring
The Supporter or the Bearer of the Earth

"He who is swift"; One who is the fastest in reaching the devotee the moment his loving heart remembers Him
Of endless appetite

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/41.sanskrit_iast:

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The Originator
The Agitator
One who revels is Deva
Containing all glories within: One in whom are all glories (Aisvarya)
The Supreme (Parama) Lord (Īśvara)
The Instrument
The Cause
The Doer

The Un-knowable
The one hidden in the cave of the heart

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: Resolute
The Basis or the Substratum
The Ultimate Authority, State or Goal
One who confers the right abode

The extremely vivid
The ever-contented one

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: That which revels in every form or that in which all yogins in their meditation revel

Passionless
The path
The Guide", the "Conductor
One who leads

The best among those who have power
Dharma itself, the law that upholds

hiraṇyagarbhaḥ śatrughno vyāpto vāyuradhokṣajaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: “One who prevents men from going astray into wrong paths (Vikunthah)."

The expanded
The golden womb, the cosmic creator
The destroyer of the enemies
The Pervader

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/45.sanskrit_iast:

ugraḥ saṃvatsaro dakṣo viśrāmo viśvadakṣiṇaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: Time as the ordered cycle of seasons

The Receiver

The proof

Omniscient
The Supreme Knowledge of all other knowledges

All-pervading
