vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/90.sanskrit_iast:
aṇurbṛhatkṛśaḥ sthūlo guṇabhṛnnirguṇo mahān |
adhṛtaḥ svadhṛtaḥ svāsyaḥ prāgvaṃśo vaṃśavardhanaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The Subtlest; the All-pervading
At the same time He is Greater than the Greatest in dimension, He being the All-pervading
One Who is lean; subtle; delicate
One Who is the fattest; the grossest; roughest
“One Who supports”—maintains and expresses through the three guṇas
Without-any-properties
The Great; the Glorious; the Mighty
None supports Him, but He supports all
Self-supported
One Who has an Effulgent Face
One Who has the most ancient ancestry
“He Who multiplies His family of descendents."

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/91.sanskrit_iast:
bhārabhṛt kathito yogī yogīśaḥ sarvakāmadaḥ |
āśramaḥ śramaṇaḥ kṣāmaḥ suparṇo vāyuvāhanaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One Who carries the load of the Universe
One Who is glorified in the Vedas and other spiritual text books
The supreme yogī, realized through yoga
The King of yogīs
One Who fulfils all desires of all true devotees
Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the harbour, the sequestered haven for all who are tossed about in the storms of life without and within
"One Who persecutes the worldly people"—who, driven by their hungers and passions, seek sense-gratifications
“One Who destroys everything during the final deluge"—He Who prunes our agitations and shrinks our desire-prompted world-projections
The Golden Leaf
The mover of the winds

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/92.sanskrit_iast:
dhanurdharo dhanurvedo daṇḍo damayitā damaḥ |
aparājitaḥ sarvasaho niyantā'niyamo'yamaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The wielder of the Bow
The revealer of archery and the unfailing technique of Oṃ-meditation
One Who punishes the wicked
The Controller
That which is ultimately gained by the worldly punishments—the final experience of Beatitude in the Self
The Invincible; One Who cannot be defeated
One Who carries the entire Universe
The supreme controller, controlled by none
One Who is not under the laws of anyone else
One Who knows no death

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/93.sanskrit_iast:
sattvavān sāttvikaḥ satyaḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ |
abhiprāyaḥ priyārho'rhaḥ priyakṛt prītivardhanaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One Who is full of exploits and courage
One Who is full of sāttvika qualities
Truth
One Who is the very abode of Truth and Righteousness
“One Who is faced by all seekers marching to the Infinite."
One Who deserves all our love
Nārāyaṇa is the One Who deserves to be worshipped by all devotees
“One Who is ever-obliging in fulfilling our wishes”—One Who is anxiously eager for the well-being of all devotees
The one who increases love and joy

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/94.sanskrit_iast:
vihāyasagatirjyotiḥ surucirhutabhugvibhuḥ |
ravirvirocanaḥ sūryaḥ savitā ravilocanaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The one whose path is the sky
Effulgent with His own inherent Light
The one of beautiful radiance and auspicious will
One Who receives and enjoys all that is offered into the sacred fire during the Vedic Rituals—yajñas and yāgas
All-pervading
One Who absorbs the vapours (Rasa) from everything
One Who shines in different forms
The sun that nurtures and nourishes all living creatures
The One Who brings forth, from Himself, the Universe of things and beings
One Whose Eyes are the Sun

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/95.sanskrit_iast:
ananto hutabhugbhoktā sukhado naikajo'grajaḥ |
anirviṇṇaḥ sadāmarṣī lokādhiṣṭhānamadbhutaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: Endless
One Who accepts the things devotedly poured as oblation into the sacred Fire
The One Who enjoys the world of objects-emotions-thoughts
One Who gives the experience of Eternal Bliss to the devotees at their final spiritual destination-mokṣa
Na—'not'; Eka—'once'; Ja -born.'
The One Who was First- Born
"One Who feels no disappointments"—Who has no chance to feel disappointment as He is ever the totally fulfilled
"One Who ever forgives the trespasses of all His devotees"—One Who is infinitely merciful and kind
The one sole substratum for the entire Universe of things and beings
Wonder is He

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/96.sanskrit_iast:
sanātsanātanatamaḥ kapilaḥ kapiravyayaḥ |
svastidaḥ svastikṛtsvasti svastibhuksvastidakṣiṇaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The Beginningless and the Endless factor is He
The most Ancient
The Lord Himself, manifested as the great ṛṣi Kapila, propounded the Sāṅkhya philosophy
One Who drinks water
"The One in Whom the entire Universe merges"—during the great deluge when the Total-mind—the Creator—rests
One Who gives Svasti to all His sincere devotees
The maker and remover of auspicious conditions
"One Who is the Source of all Auspiciousness"—as He is Himself the Auspicious
"One Who constantly lives in His Experience a perpetual sense of holy Auspiciousness"-as it is His very nature-divine
Lord is ever engaged in smartly distributing Auspiciousness

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/97.sanskrit_iast:
araudraḥ kuṇḍalī cakrī vikramyūrjitaśāsanaḥ |
śabdātigaḥ śabdasahaḥ śiśiraḥ śarvarīkaraḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One Who has none of the negative terrible urges and emotions
The wearer of makara earrings
The bearer of the discus Sudarśana
He Who is more daring than all others
“One Who commands and administers with His Hand."
"He Who transcends all words"—One Who is Indescribable
The one who permits invocation through sacred sound
The cool season that relieves burning heat
The maker of night and darkness

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/98.sanskrit_iast:
akrūraḥ peśalo dakṣo dakṣiṇaḥ kṣamiṇāṃvaraḥ |
vidvattamo vītabhayaḥ puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: Never-cruel
One Who is supremely soft
The prompt and capable one
One Who is most liberal
One Who has the greatest amount of patience with the sinners and for-giveness for their sins
“One Who has the greatest Wisdom."
One Who has lost all fears
“One Whose Glory when ‘heard’ (sravana) and ‘sung’ (keertana) causes merits (punya) to grow in the bosom of that devotee

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/99.sanskrit_iast:
uttāraṇo duṣkṛtihā puṇyo duḥsvapnanāśanaḥ |
vīrahā rakṣaṇaḥ santo jīvanaḥ paryavasthitaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One Who lifts us out of the ocean-of-change
The destroyer of evil deeds
Supremely Pure
One Who destroys all 'bad dreams'
One Who ends the passage from womb-to-womb—the wheel of birth and death
One Who is the Protector of the Universe
The one present as the good and saintly
The Life — Spark in all living creatures
In all places, in all creatures, He dwells

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/100.sanskrit_iast:
anantarūpo'nantaśrīrjitamanyurbhayāpahaḥ |
caturaśro gabhīrātmā vidiśo vyādiśo diśaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One of Infinite Forms
“One Who is full of Infinite Glories,” or, “One Who is full of Incomparable Powers."
“One Who has conquered anger" (manyuh)
One Who destroys or removes all fears in samsaric life
One Who deals squarely with all
One Who, in His Real Nature, is too deep to be fathomed by the frail instrument of our mind
One Who is unique in His giving
One Who is unique in His Commanding — Power
One Who advises and gives knowledge

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/101.sanskrit_iast:
anādirbhūrbhuvo lakṣmīḥ suvīro rucirāṅgadaḥ |
janano janajanmādirbhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: "One Who is the First Cause" -and Who is Himself the Uncaused
The very substratum or support for the Earth
One Who is the wealth, the richness or glory of the Universe
One Who moves through various ways which are all divinely glorious
The wearer of resplendent shoulder-caps
He Who delivers all living creatures
One Who is the sole Cause of birth for all living creatures in the Universe
“One Whose form is terrible and frightening to the sinners."
“One Whose prowess is irresistible and fearful to His enemies."

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/102.sanskrit_iast:
ādhāranilayo'dhātā puṣpahāsaḥ prajāgaraḥ |
ūrdhvagaḥ satpathācāraḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ paṇaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: “One Who is the fundamental sustainer"—the support for all that exists
The unsurpassed supreme controller
He Who shines like an opening flower
"Ever — Awakened"—He Who knows no sleep
The exalted one
“One Who walks the path of truth”—a path which others implicitly follow to reach the Truth Infinite
One Who gives 'prāṇa' to all
Therefore, Śrī Nārāyaṇa is called 'praṇavaḥ': meaning He is of the 'nature of oṃkāra.'
The Supreme Manager of the Universe

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/103.sanskrit_iast:
pramāṇaṃ prāṇanilayaḥ prāṇabhṛtprāṇajīvanaḥ |
tattvaṃ tattvavidekātmā janmamṛtyujarātigaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: “He Whose very form is the Vedas"—which are the only 'proof' for the Eternal Reality
He in Whom all ‘prāṇas’ stand established
"He Who rules over all 'Pragnas' "-Śrī Hari is the One Who causes everyone to eat
He Who maintains the life-breath in all living creatures
"The Reality"—That which is Eternal, the Essence
The knower of reality as it truly is
The one Self
“One Who knows no change or modifications in Himself."

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/104.sanskrit_iast:
bhūrbhuvaḥsvastarustāraḥ savitā prapitāmahaḥ |
yajño yajñapatiryajvā yajñāṅgo yajñavāhanaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One Who is the Sap in the Tree-of — Life existing in all this Universe of the higher-world, our-world and the lower-world
"One Who helps all to crossover"—the Eternal Boat-man, to Whom, if the devotees can surrender in unswerving faith and true devotion
"He Who is the Father of All"- Who is the Eternal Father of the entire Universe
“He Who is the Father of even the ‘Father of all Beings,’ the Creator, Brahmājī, of the Trinity."
One Whose very nature is yajña
The Lord of all yajñas
The One Who performs yajña according to the strict prescriptions laid down in the Vedas
One Whose limbs are the ‘things’ employed in yajña
“One Who fulfils yajñas in complete and exact accord with the Vedic instructions."

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/105.sanskrit_iast:
yajñabhṛd yajñakṛd yajñī yajñabhug yajñasādhanaḥ |
yajñāntakṛd yajñaguhyamannamannāda eva ca ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: The ruler of yajñas
“One Who performs yajña."
One Who is the constant 'Enjoyer' of the perpetual yajñas
One receiver of all that is offered
“One Who fulfils all yajñas."
“One Who performs the last, concluding act in all yajñas."
Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the most profound truth to be realised in all yajñas
“One Who has Himself become the 'food' "-sense-objects which are the 'food' consumed by the sense-organs
One Who eats the 'food

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/106.sanskrit_iast:
ātmayoniḥ svayañjāto vaikhānaḥ sāmagāyanaḥ |
devakīnandanaḥ sraṣṭā kṣitīśaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: Self-born
Self-born
The Boar who dug through the earth to destroy Hiraṇyākṣa
One Who sings the Sāma-songs
He Who appeared as born to Devakī in His Incarnation as Kṛṣṇa
One Who creates
One Who is the Lord of the Earth
Meditating upon Whom, all vāsanās (sins) are liquidated

vyasa/vishnu-sahasranama/stanza/107.sanskrit_iast:
śaṅkhabhṛnnandakī cakrī śārṅgadhanvā gadādharaḥ |
rathāṅgapāṇirakṣobhyaḥ sarvapraharaṇāyudhaḥ ||

chinmayananda/thousand-ways-to-the-trans.english_close: One Who has the divine conch named Pāñcajanya
The bearer of the sword Nandaka
The bearer of the discus Sudarśana
The wielder of the bow Śārṅga
The mace-bearer
The one whose hand holds the chariot wheel
One Who cannot be exasperated by anyone, by any act or acts, however blasphemous they may be
“He Who has all implements for all kinds of assault and fight."

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
दामव्यालकटन्यायो मा ते भवतु राघव |
भीमभासदृढस्थित्या तवास्त्वतिविशोकता ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
dāmavyālakaṭanyāyo mā te bhavatu rāghava |
bhīmabhāsadṛḍhasthityā tavāstvativiśokatā ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: The pattern of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa may not become yours, descendant of Raghu; through the firm stance of Bhīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha, let there be for you complete freedom from sorrow.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
दामव्यालकटन्यायो भीमभासदृढस्थितिः |
ब्रह्मन्किमुक्तं भवता भवतापापहारिणा ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
dāmavyālakaṭanyāyo bhīmabhāsadṛḍhasthitiḥ |
brahmankimuktaṃ bhavatā bhavatāpāpahāriṇā ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: The pattern of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa and the firm stance of Bhīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha—O brahman, what has been said by you, remover of the affliction of becoming?

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
दामव्यालकटन्यायं मीमभासदृढस्थितिम् |
शृणु राघव तच्छ्रुत्वा यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
dāmavyālakaṭanyāyaṃ mīmabhāsadṛḍhasthitim |
śṛṇu rāghava tacchrutvā yathecchasi tathā kuru ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Hear the pattern of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa and the firm stance of Mīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha, descendant of Raghu; having heard that, act as you wish.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
आसीत्पातालकुहरे सर्वैश्वर्यमनोहरे |
शम्बरो नाम दैत्येन्द्रो मायामणिमहार्णवः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
āsītpātālakuhare sarvaiśvaryamanohare |
śambaro nāma daityendro māyāmaṇimahārṇavaḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: In a cavern of the underworld captivating through every lordly power, there was Śambara by name, lord of the Daityas, a great ocean of māyā-jewels.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
तस्यादिदेवदेवस्य कठिनोड्डामराकृतेः |
बभूव विपुलं सैन्यमासुरं सुरनाशनम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
tasyādidevadevasya kaṭhinoḍḍāmarākṛteḥ |
babhūva vipulaṃ sainyamāsuraṃ suranāśanam ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: For that one, lord of the primordial gods, whose form was hard and fearsome, there came to be a vast Asuric army, destroyer of the gods.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
तस्मिन्मायाबले सुप्ते देशान्तरगते तथा |
तत्सैन्यं तरसा जघ्नुश्छिद्रं प्राप्य किलामराः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
tasminmāyābale supte deśāntaragate tathā |
tatsainyaṃ tarasā jaghnuśchidraṃ prāpya kilāmarāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: While he, whose strength was māyā, slept and likewise was away in another land, the immortals, having found an opening, indeed destroyed his army by force.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
अथ शम्बरदैत्येन मुण्डिकाङ्कद्रुमादयः |
रक्षार्थं मन्त्रिसामन्ताः स्वसेनासु नियोजिताः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
atha śambaradaityena muṇḍikāṅkadrumādayaḥ |
rakṣārthaṃ mantrisāmantāḥ svasenāsu niyojitāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Then Muṇḍikāṅka, Druma, and the others, as ministers and subordinate chiefs, were appointed by the Daitya Śambara within his own armies for protection.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
तानप्यन्तरमासाद्य जघ्नुर्देवा भयानकान् |
स्वयं कोपादथायासीच्छम्बरः सुरपत्तनम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
tānapyantaramāsādya jaghnurdevā bhayānakān |
svayaṃ kopādathāyāsīcchambaraḥ surapattanam ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: The gods, having found an opening, killed even those fearsome ones; then Śambara himself, in anger, went toward the city of the gods.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
तस्य मायाबलाद्भीताः सुरास्तेऽन्तर्धिमाययुः |
मेरुकाननकुञ्जेषु भयभारावयन्त्रिताः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
tasya māyābalādbhītāḥ surāste'ntardhimāyayuḥ |
merukānanakuñjeṣu bhayabhārāvayantritāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Those gods, afraid of the force of his māyā, went into concealment in the bowers of Meru's forests, constricted by the weight of fear.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
क्रन्दत्क्षुद्रामरगणं बाष्पक्लिन्नाङ्गनामुखम् |
शून्यं ददर्श स स्वर्गं कल्पक्षीणजगत्समम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
krandatkṣudrāmaragaṇaṃ bāṣpaklinnāṅganāmukham |
śūnyaṃ dadarśa sa svargaṃ kalpakṣīṇajagatsamam ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: He saw heaven empty, its bands of lesser immortals crying, the faces of its women wet with tears, like a world depleted at a kalpa's exhaustion.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
विहृत्य कुपितस्तत्र दोर्दण्डमदघूर्णितः |
लोकपालपुरीं दग्ध्वा जगामात्मीयमालयम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
vihṛtya kupitastatra dordaṇḍamadaghūrṇitaḥ |
lokapālapurīṃ dagdhvā jagāmātmīyamālayam ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Having ranged about there, angry and reeling with pride in his staff-like arms, having burned the city of the world-guardians, he went to his own abode.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
एवं दृढतरीभूते द्वेषे दानवदेवयोः |
देवाः स्वर्गं परित्यज्य दिक्षु जग्मुरदर्शनम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ dṛḍhatarībhūte dveṣe dānavadevayoḥ |
devāḥ svargaṃ parityajya dikṣu jagmuradarśanam ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Thus, when the hatred between the Dānavas and the gods had grown still firmer, the gods, having abandoned heaven, went out of sight in every direction.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
अथ शम्बरदैत्येन ये ये सेनाधिनायकाः |
क्रियन्ते यत्नतस्तांस्ताञ्जघ्नुर्यत्नपराः सुराः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
atha śambaradaityena ye ye senādhināyakāḥ |
kriyante yatnatastāṃstāñjaghnuryatnaparāḥ surāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Then, whichever army-commanders are appointed by the Daitya Śambara with effort, the gods, intent on their endeavor, killed each and every one.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
यावदुद्वेगमापन्नः शम्बरः कोपवान्भृशम् |
ससर्ज मायया घोरानसुरांस्त्रीन्महाबलान् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
yāvadudvegamāpannaḥ śambaraḥ kopavānbhṛśam |
sasarja māyayā ghorānasurāṃstrīnmahābalān ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: At last, Śambara, having fallen into agitation and exceedingly angry, created through māyā three terrible Asuras of great strength.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
निर्मिता मायया भीमाः पक्षक्षुब्धा इवाद्रयः |
उदगुस्ते महामाया दामो व्यालः कटस्तथा ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
nirmitā māyayā bhīmāḥ pakṣakṣubdhā ivādrayaḥ |
udaguste mahāmāyā dāmo vyālaḥ kaṭastathā ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Fashioned by māyā, terrible, like mountains with their wings heaving, those possessors of great māyā arose: Dāma, Vyāla, Kaṭa likewise.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
वासनात्माभिमानाभ्यां हीनास्ते प्रथमोद्गताः |
नाभिपातं न वापातं न विदुस्ते पलायनम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
vāsanātmābhimānābhyāṃ hīnāste prathamodgatāḥ |
nābhipātaṃ na vāpātaṃ na viduste palāyanam ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: At their first arising, they were devoid of vāsanā and self-identification; they knew neither attack, nor falling back, nor flight.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
न जीवितं न मरणं समरे न जयाजयौ |
केवलं सैनिकानग्रे दृष्ट्वा ते हननोद्यताः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
na jīvitaṃ na maraṇaṃ samare na jayājayau |
kevalaṃ sainikānagre dṛṣṭvā te hananodyatāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Neither life nor death, in battle neither victory nor defeat; only, having seen the soldiers before them, they were intent on killing.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
शम्बरश्चिन्तयामास परितुष्टमनास्तदा |
इष्टानिष्टाभिरेते हि वासनाभिर्यदुज्झिताः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
śambaraścintayāmāsa parituṣṭamanāstadā |
iṣṭāniṣṭābhirete hi vāsanābhiryadujjhitāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Śambara reflected, his manas fully satisfied, then: ‘Since these indeed are forsaken by desired and undesired vāsanās—

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
तदेते न पलायन्ते देवैरभिहता अपि |
इति निर्णीय दैत्येन्द्रो दामव्यालकटान्विताम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
tadete na palāyante devairabhihatā api |
iti nirṇīya daityendro dāmavyālakaṭānvitām ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: therefore these do not flee, even when struck by the gods’—having determined thus, the lord of the Daityas: an army accompanied by Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa—

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
सेनां संप्रेषयामास देवेन्द्रबलघातिनीम् |
दैत्याः सागरकुञ्जेभ्यः कन्दरेभ्यश्च सायुधाः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
senāṃ saṃpreṣayāmāsa devendrabalaghātinīm |
daityāḥ sāgarakuñjebhyaḥ kandarebhyaśca sāyudhāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: —that army he dispatched, striking Indra’s force; the Daityas, armed, from the ocean-groves and from the caverns—

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
उदगुर्भीमनिर्ह्रादाः सपक्षगिरिलीलया |
अथोत्तस्थुर्निकुञ्जेभ्यः कन्दरेभ्यः सुरा बलात् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
udagurbhīmanirhrādāḥ sapakṣagirilīlayā |
athottasthurnikuñjebhyaḥ kandarebhyaḥ surā balāt ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: —came forth with terrible roars, with the play of winged mountains; then the gods rose up from the bowers and from the caverns, forcefully—

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
प्रयान्त इव शैलेन्द्रा भीमाः स्वर्वासिनां गणाः |
देवासुरपताकिन्योस्तद्युद्धमभवत्तयोः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
prayānta iva śailendrā bhīmāḥ svarvāsināṃ gaṇāḥ |
devāsurapatākinyostadyuddhamabhavattayoḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: —the hosts of heaven-dwellers, formidable, advancing like lords of mountains; that battle of the armies of gods and Asuras arose between the two—

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
अकालोल्बणकल्पान्तभीषणं भुवनान्तरे |
तस्मिंस्तदा वर्तमाने घोरे समरसंभ्रमे ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
akālolbaṇakalpāntabhīṣaṇaṃ bhuvanāntare |
tasmiṃstadā vartamāne ghore samarasaṃbhrame ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: —untimely, excessive, and terrifying as the end of an aeon within the world; when that terrible turmoil of battle was underway then—

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
पतिताङ्गायुधानीह प्रस्रवद्रुधिराणि च |
पयांसीव विशीर्णानि देवसैन्यानि दुद्रुवुः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
patitāṅgāyudhānīha prasravadrudhirāṇi ca |
payāṃsīva viśīrṇāni devasainyāni dudruvuḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: —the armies of the gods, their limbs and weapons fallen and their blood streaming, fled here, scattered like waters.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
दामव्यालकटास्तानि चिरमन्तर्हितान्यपि |
अनुजग्मुर्लसन्नादमिन्धनानीव पावकाः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
dāmavyālakaṭāstāni ciramantarhitānyapi |
anujagmurlasannādamindhanānīva pāvakāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa followed those armies for a long time, even when hidden, with a resounding roar, as fires follow fuel.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
अन्विष्यन्तोऽपि यत्नेन नालभन्तासुराः सुरान् |
अलब्धेष्वमरौघेषु दामव्यालकटास्तथा ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
anviṣyanto'pi yatnena nālabhantāsurāḥ surān |
alabdheṣvamaraugheṣu dāmavyālakaṭāstathā ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Though seeking with effort, the Asuras did not find the gods; when the hosts of immortals were not found, Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa then—

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
जग्मुः पातालकोशस्थं प्रभुं प्रमुदिताशयाः |
अथ देवा विषण्णास्ते क्षणमाश्वास्य वै ययुः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
jagmuḥ pātālakośasthaṃ prabhuṃ pramuditāśayāḥ |
atha devā viṣaṇṇāste kṣaṇamāśvāsya vai yayuḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: —their inner dispositions delighted, they went to the lord dwelling in the vault of the underworld; then the despondent gods, having recovered their breath for a moment, indeed went—

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
दामादिभिश्च विजिता ब्रह्माणममितौजसम् |
तेषामाविरभूद्ब्रह्मा रक्तो रक्तासनच्छविः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
dāmādibhiśca vijitā brahmāṇamamitaujasam |
teṣāmāvirabhūdbrahmā rakto raktāsanacchaviḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: —and, conquered by Dāma and the others, to Brahmā of unmeasured vigor; Brahmā became manifest before them, red, with the radiance of a red seat.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
प्रणेमुस्ते सुरास्तस्मै तत्सर्वं शम्बरेहितम् |
सम्यक्प्रकथयामासुर्दामव्यालकटक्रमम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
praṇemuste surāstasmai tatsarvaṃ śambarehitam |
samyakprakathayāmāsurdāmavyālakaṭakramam ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Those gods bowed down to him; fully they related all that was contrived by Śambara: the course of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
समाकर्ण्याखिलं ब्रह्मा विचार्य स विचारवान् |
उवाचेदं सुरानीकमाश्वासनपरं वचः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
samākarṇyākhilaṃ brahmā vicārya sa vicāravān |
uvācedaṃ surānīkamāśvāsanaparaṃ vacaḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Having heard everything, Brahmā, having considered, reflective—he spoke this reassurance-centered word to the host of gods.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
हन्त वर्षसहस्रान्ते शम्बरस्य रणे सुराः |
जेतव्या समरे सेना तावत्कालं प्रतीक्ष्यताम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
hanta varṣasahasrānte śambarasya raṇe surāḥ |
jetavyā samare senā tāvatkālaṃ pratīkṣyatām ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Now, O gods, let there be waiting for that span of time. At the end of a thousand years, Śambara's army must be conquered in battle, in combat.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
दामव्यालकटानेतान्युध्यध्वममरेश्वराः |
योधयन्तः पलायध्वं युद्धार्थं पुनरेव च ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
dāmavyālakaṭānetānyudhyadhvamamareśvarāḥ |
yodhayantaḥ palāyadhvaṃ yuddhārthaṃ punareva ca ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Fight these—Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa, O lords of the immortals. And while making them fight, flee again, precisely for the sake of battle.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
युद्धाभ्यासबलादेषा मुकुराणामिवाशये |
अहङ्कारचमत्कारः प्रतिबिम्बमुपैष्यति ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
yuddhābhyāsabalādeṣā mukurāṇāmivāśaye |
ahaṅkāracamatkāraḥ pratibimbamupaiṣyati ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: From the force of battle-practice, this striking manifestation of I-making will acquire a reflection in the inner seat, like mirrors.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
गृहीतवासना ह्येते दामव्यालकटासुराः |
सुजेया वो भविष्यन्ति लग्नजालाः खगा इव ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
gṛhītavāsanā hyete dāmavyālakaṭāsurāḥ |
sujeyā vo bhaviṣyanti lagnajālāḥ khagā iva ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: These Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa demons, having acquired vāsanā, indeed will become easily conquerable for you, like birds with nets fastened to them.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
आस्थामात्रमनन्तनां दुःखानामाकरं विदुः |
अनास्थामात्रमभितः सुखानामाकरं विदुः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
āsthāmātramanantanāṃ duḥkhānāmākaraṃ viduḥ |
anāsthāmātramabhitaḥ sukhānāmākaraṃ viduḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: They know mere attachment as a mine of sorrows without end; they know mere non-attachment, on every side, as a mine of pleasures.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
वासनातन्तुबद्धोऽयं लोको हि परिवर्तते |
सा प्रवृद्धातिदुःखाय सुखायोच्छेदमागता ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
vāsanātantubaddho'yaṃ loko hi parivartate |
sā pravṛddhātiduḥkhāya sukhāyocchedamāgatā ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: This world, bound by the thread of vāsanā, indeed turns round. It, having grown, is for extreme sorrow; having come to cessation, it is for pleasure.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
धीरोऽप्यतिबहुज्ञोऽपि प्रवृद्धोऽपि महानपि |
तृष्णया बध्यते जन्तुः सिंहः शृङ्खलया यथा ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
dhīro'pyatibahujño'pi pravṛddho'pi mahānapi |
tṛṣṇayā badhyate jantuḥ siṃhaḥ śṛṅkhalayā yathā ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: A creature, even steadfast, even knowing very much, even fully grown, even great, is bound by tṛṣṇā, as a lion by a chain.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्देवस्तत्रैवान्तर्धिमाययौ |
सुरास्त्वाकर्ण्य तद्वाक्यं जग्मुश्चाभिमतां दिशम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
ityuktvā bhagavāndevastatraivāntardhimāyayau |
surāstvākarṇya tadvākyaṃ jagmuścābhimatāṃ diśam ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Thus having spoken, the blessed god went into disappearance there itself; and the gods, in turn, having heard that statement, went to the desired direction.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
चक्रुर्दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषं प्रलयाभ्ररवोपमम् |
अथ दैत्यैर्महाव्योम्नि तैः पातालतलोत्थितैः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
cakrurdundubhinirghoṣaṃ pralayābhraravopamam |
atha daityairmahāvyomni taiḥ pātālatalotthitaiḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: They made a kettledrum roar like the roar of a cloud at dissolution. Then, in the vast sky, by those demons risen from the floor of the underworld—

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
कालक्षेपकरं घोरं पुनर्युद्धमवर्तत |
पुनः पलायनं चक्रुरयुध्यन्त पुनः सुराः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
kālakṣepakaraṃ ghoraṃ punaryuddhamavartata |
punaḥ palāyanaṃ cakrurayudhyanta punaḥ surāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Again a war, dreadful, causing time to pass, occurred. Again the gods took flight; again they fought.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
एवं ते कालहरणं युद्धेन सुरपुङ्गवाः |
चक्रुर्नानाविधोपायैर्दैत्यव्यामोहकारणात् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ te kālaharaṇaṃ yuddhena surapuṅgavāḥ |
cakrurnānāvidhopāyairdaityavyāmohakāraṇāt ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Thus those bulls among the gods effected the taking-away of time through battle, by various kinds of expedients, for causing bewilderment among the demons.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
एतावता च कालेन दृढाभ्यासादहंकृतेः |
दामादयोऽहमित्यास्थां जगृहुर्युक्तचेतसः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
etāvatā ca kālena dṛḍhābhyāsādahaṃkṛteḥ |
dāmādayo'hamityāsthāṃ jagṛhuryuktacetasaḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: And over this much time, from firm repetition of I-making, Dāma and the others, their minds yoked, took up the attachment 'I' as such.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
भववासनया ग्रस्ता मोहवासनया युताः |
आशापाशनिबद्धास्ते ततः कृपणतां गताः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
bhavavāsanayā grastā mohavāsanayā yutāḥ |
āśāpāśanibaddhāste tataḥ kṛpaṇatāṃ gatāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Seized by the vāsanā of becoming and joined to the vāsanā of delusion, they, bound by the snare of hope, then went into wretchedness.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
स्थिरो भवतु मे देहः सुखायास्तु धनं मम |
इति वृद्धधियां तेषां धैर्यमन्तर्धिमाययौ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
sthiro bhavatu me dehaḥ sukhāyāstu dhanaṃ mama |
iti vṛddhadhiyāṃ teṣāṃ dhairyamantardhimāyayau ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: “May my body be stable; for pleasure, may wealth be mine”; as such thoughts grew in them, their courage disappeared.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
अतस्तस्मिन् रणे दैत्याः सापेक्षत्वमुपाययुः |
मरिष्यामो मरिष्याम इति चिन्ताहताशयाः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
atastasmin raṇe daityāḥ sāpekṣatvamupāyayuḥ |
mariṣyāmo mariṣyāma iti cintāhatāśayāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Therefore, in that battle, the Daityas, their inner dispositions struck by the thought “We shall die, we shall die,” came to a state of anxious concern.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
अथ प्रम्लानसत्त्वास्ते हन्तुमग्रगतं भटम् |
न शेकुरिन्धने क्षीणे हविर्दग्धमिवाग्नयः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
atha pramlānasattvāste hantumagragataṃ bhaṭam |
na śekurindhane kṣīṇe havirdagdhamivāgnayaḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Then they, their vitality withered, could not kill the warrior gone to the front—like fires: fuel exhausted, the oblation burned.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन मरणाद्भीतचेतसः |
पलायनैकशरणा नष्टास्ते त्रिदशारयः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
bahunātra kimuktena maraṇādbhītacetasaḥ |
palāyanaikaśaraṇā naṣṭāste tridaśārayaḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: What need is there to say much here? Those enemies of the Thirty, their minds frightened by death and having flight as their sole refuge, were ruined.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
अहमेतत्प्रबोधाय वच्मि राम महामते |
दामव्यालकटन्यायो मा भवत्विति लीलया ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
ahametatprabodhāya vacmi rāma mahāmate |
dāmavyālakaṭanyāyo mā bhavatviti līlayā ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: I say this for awakening, O Rāma of great understanding, playfully: “Let the Dāma–Vyāla–Kaṭa pattern not come to be.”

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
अविवेकानुसंधानाच्चित्तमापदमीदृशीम् |
अनन्तभवदुःखाय परिगृह्णाति हेलया ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
avivekānusaṃdhānāccittamāpadamīdṛśīm |
anantabhavaduḥkhāya parigṛhṇāti helayā ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Through continued engagement with non-discernment, citta heedlessly takes on a calamity such as this, for the sorrow of endless becoming.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
कथं दामकटव्यालाः समुत्पन्नाः परात्पदात् |
इति मे संशयं ब्रह्मन्यथावच्छेत्तुमर्हसि ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
kathaṃ dāmakaṭavyālāḥ samutpannāḥ parātpadāt |
iti me saṃśayaṃ brahmanyathāvacchettumarhasi ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: “How did Dāma, Kaṭa, and Vyāla arise from the supreme state?” This is my doubt, O Brahmin; you should cut it away exactly as it is.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
यथा दामादयो राम प्रतिभामात्ररूपिणः |
तथैवेमे वयमिति न बहिः क्वापि संस्थिताः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
yathā dāmādayo rāma pratibhāmātrarūpiṇaḥ |
tathaiveme vayamiti na bahiḥ kvāpi saṃsthitāḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Just as Dāma and the others, O Rāma, have forms consisting only of pratibhā, so too these whom we call “we” are not established externally, anywhere at all.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
अलीकमेव त्वद्भावो मद्भावोऽलीकमेव च |
दामव्यालकटादीनां सद्भावोऽलीकमेव च ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
alīkameva tvadbhāvo madbhāvo'līkameva ca |
dāmavyālakaṭādīnāṃ sadbhāvo'līkameva ca ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Your being is wholly unreal; my being is wholly unreal too; and the actual being of Dāma, Vyāla, Kaṭa, and the others is wholly unreal too.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
प्रतिभासमयी काचिज्जीवशक्तिः परात्मनः |
शम्बरध्यानविक्षुब्धा त्रिधोल्लासमवाप सा ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
pratibhāsamayī kācijjīvaśaktiḥ parātmanaḥ |
śambaradhyānavikṣubdhā tridhollāsamavāpa sā ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: A certain life-power of the supreme self, consisting of pratibhāsa and stirred by Śambara’s meditation—it attained a threefold flashing-forth.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
तस्मान्नेमे वयं सत्या न च दामादयः क्वचित् |
सत्यं संवेदनं शुद्धं बोधाकाशं निरञ्जनम् ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
tasmānneme vayaṃ satyā na ca dāmādayaḥ kvacit |
satyaṃ saṃvedanaṃ śuddhaṃ bodhākāśaṃ nirañjanam ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Therefore, these ‘we’ are not real; nor are Dāma and the others real anywhere; real is saṃvedana, pure, bodhākāśa, unstained.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
सत्यं सर्वगतं शान्तमस्त्यनस्तमनोदयम् |
तस्य शक्तिसमुल्लासमात्रं जगदिति स्थितिः ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
satyaṃ sarvagataṃ śāntamastyanastamanodayam |
tasya śaktisamullāsamātraṃ jagaditi sthitiḥ ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: The real, present everywhere, stilled, with an arising that has no setting, exists; the world is only the full flashing-forth of its śakti—this is the settled account.

gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_devanagari:
सर्वत्र सर्वमिदमस्ति यथाभूतं नो किंचन क्वचिदिहास्ति न चानुभूतम् |
शान्तं सदेकमिदमाननमित्थमास्ते
संत्यक्तशङ्कमपभेदमतस्त्वमास्स्व ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.sanskrit_iast:
sarvatra sarvamidamasti yathābhūtaṃ no kiṃcana kvacidihāsti na cānubhūtam |
śāntaṃ sadekamidamānanamitthamāste
saṃtyaktaśaṅkamapabhedamatastvamāssva ||
gauda-abhinanda/laghu-yogavasistha/sthit.english_close: Everywhere, all this exists just as it has become; if it is not experienced, nothing whatever exists anywhere here; the one stilled being, this face, remains thus; therefore, you remain, with doubt abandoned and division put away.

shankara/upadesa-sahasri/category-self-r.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
shankara/upadesa-sahasri/category-self-r.evidence_note: Intrinsic consciousness is distinguished from reflected mental presentation and a correcting cognition; variations of the reflecting medium do not become intrinsic changes in the Self.
shankara/upadesa-sahasri/category-self-r.notes: The formal fragment does not derive every regress, sleep argument, or lexical rule. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

vacaspati/bhamati/category-bhamati.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
vacaspati/bhamati/category-bhamati.evidence_note: Ignorance, its locus and its explanatory support must be distinguished; the differentiated jīva account includes preparation and corrective cognition.
vacaspati/bhamati/category-bhamati.notes: Mirror and delimitation language are not interchangeable physical models; separate whole Bhāmatī theory remains future work. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

prakasatman/pancapadika-vivarana/categor.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
prakasatman/pancapadika-vivarana/categor.evidence_note: Illumination by consciousness does not by itself oppose ignorance; the positive explanatory account distinguishes support, illusory presentation, and correcting knowledge.
prakasatman/pancapadika-vivarana/categor.notes: Main Vivaraṇa text is distinguished from the edition’s notes and embedded Pañcapādikā. Selected Sanskrit scan pages independently inspected; Rāmaśāstrī Bhāgavatācārya edition, Benares1892.

madhusudana/siddhanta-bindu/category-bin.locus: First-stanza commentary: alternative accounts of jīva, reflection and ignorance
madhusudana/siddhanta-bindu/category-bin.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
madhusudana/siddhanta-bindu/category-bin.evidence_note: Several explanatory models are presented; a presentation of alternatives does not erase Madhusūdana’s own preferences or turn every option into one doctrine.
madhusudana/siddhanta-bindu/category-bin.notes: The study reconstructs selected mechanisms, not a complete independent model of each alternative. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

saccidanandendra/vedantaprakriyapratyabh.locus: PartI printed277–282,536–546; compare Mūlāvidyānirāsa III117–141 and conclusion
saccidanandendra/vedantaprakriyapratyabh.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
saccidanandendra/vedantaprakriyapratyabh.evidence_note: The criticism rejects an additional positive root-ignorance explanation and challenges unexamined causal order beyond superimposition; correction does not destroy intrinsic consciousness.
saccidanandendra/vedantaprakriyapratyabh.notes: This is Saccidānandendra’s argument, not an established verdict that only his reading recovers Śaṅkara. Institutional public Sanskrit edition, selected printed pages visually checked; publisher-controlled full text not reproduced.

ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/category-rama.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain independently reviewed; the selected mathematical reconstruction has a separate review. No quotation certification or complete-work/system certification.
ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/category-rama.evidence_note: Body and indwelling self ground qualified common reference without transferring the dependent bearer’s defects to Brahman; dependence is compatible with real agency. Sections17–21 explicitly extend all words’ denotation to the supreme qualified by conscious and nonconscious reality: ordinary uptake grasps only part of what is denoted, and hearing Vedānta completes that understanding while preserving different grounds of word application.
ramanuja/vedartha-samgraha/category-rama.notes: Contextual evidence can warrant recognizing qualified reference; it is not a necessary condition that first creates Brahman-reference. The word’s application-ground, full qualified referent and the hearer’s partial grasp remain distinct. The selected formal naming rule has a reviewed derivation; complete compositional semantics and equivalence of whole school systems are not established. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

nimbarka/vedanta-parijata-saurabha/categ.locus: 1.4.20–22 and2.3.42–45 with Śrīnivāsa’s Vedāntakaustubha;1932 edition, printed139–141,235–237
nimbarka/vedanta-parijata-saurabha/categ.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain independently reviewed; the selected mathematical reconstruction has a separate review. No quotation certification or complete-work/system certification.
nimbarka/vedanta-parijata-saurabha/categ.evidence_note: Natural nonseparation and difference must be considered together: nonseparation is not postponed until release, and individual distinction is not simply canceled there. Śrīnivāsa’s opening reply at1.4.20 explicitly invokes the supreme’s denotability by all words, grounded in universal causality and related features; the Maitreyī discussion further argues through cause/effect nonotherness and the indwelling-controller relation, without indiscriminate transfer of individual defects.
nimbarka/vedanta-parijata-saurabha/categ.notes: Root Saurabha and Śrīnivāsa’s Kaustubha are separate voices, including reports of earlier teachers. The broad denotation premise is not reduced to an isolated contextual exception or merely unrealized possibility. This selection does not develop Rāmānuja’s same partial-uptake/completion explanation or resolve every compositional and pragmatic case. The selected reference derivation does not establish complete school equivalence. Selected pages of1932 combined Sanskrit print witness visually inspected; Dhundhiraja Shastri edition.

bhaskara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/category-bh.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
bhaskara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/category-bh.evidence_note: Conditioned agency is real; intrinsic unconditioned doership is denied. Removing the condition does not reduce final fulfillment to mere absence.
bhaskara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/category-bh.notes: The separate-mukta position provisionally granted in4.4 is not silently treated as his accepted final position. Selected Sanskrit page images inspected in1991 reprint of Vindhyeśvarīprasāda Dvivedin edition; OCR used only for discovery.

vallabha/tattvartha-dipa-nibandha/catego.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
vallabha/tattvartha-dipa-nibandha/catego.evidence_note: Common Hari reality is articulated through manifestation roles; concealment does not destroy intrinsic bliss, and knowledge and devotion have differentiated attainments.
vallabha/tattvartha-dipa-nibandha/catego.notes: The principal-jīva passage is not generalized to all persons. Later lower ṭippaṇī and Āvaraṇabhaṅga are not attributed to Vallabha. Selected root and upper Prakāśa in layered Sanskrit scan, Vikrama1999 edition, printed70–75; visually inspected.

vallabha/siddhanta-muktavali/category-va.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
vallabha/siddhanta-muktavali/category-va.evidence_note: Service is positively directed activity in the selected devotional instruction.
vallabha/siddhanta-muktavali/category-va.notes: This short instruction does not constitute a complete Puṣṭimārga psychology or grace theory. Received volunteer Sanskrit transcription, P.S.A. Easwaran proofreading; not independently print-collated.

madhva/tattvaviveka/category-madhva-depe.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
madhva/tattvaviveka/category-madhva-depe.evidence_note: Independence and dependence divide knowables; dependent consciousness includes never-bound Śrī. Dependence therefore does not entail bondage.
madhva/tattvaviveka/category-madhva-depe.notes: This selected argument does not make Madhva’s enduring individual distinctions merely provisional. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

madhva/anuvyakhyana/category-madhva-self.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
madhva/anuvyakhyana/category-madhva-self.evidence_note: First-person recognition, ownership and divine intrinsic articulation require distinct treatment; identical generic qualities alone do not settle subject identity.
madhva/anuvyakhyana/category-madhva-self.notes: The model covers selected arguments, not the full explanatory metaphysics of viśeṣa. Jayatīrtha’s commentary is identified separately. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

jiva/sat-sandarbha/category-jiva-love.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
jiva/sat-sandarbha/category-jiva-love.evidence_note: Love involves a specifically articulated divine potency and reciprocity, beyond a bare predicate of liberation; higher selfhood and nonfragmentary participation do not abolish individual subjects.
jiva/sat-sandarbha/category-jiva-love.notes: The formal fragment preserves participant distinction but is not a complete rasa theory. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

baladeva/govinda-bhasya/category-baladev.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/category-baladev.evidence_note: The self manifests to itself rather than merely being visible like a lamp; dependent jīva agency is real and need not bind. The argument distinguishes agency from suffering-producing guṇa association, while reserving universal governance.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/category-baladev.notes: Author’s replies are distinguished from objections and later rpc/hds editorial markers. Institutional electronic Sanskrit witness, selected connected arguments; no independent print collation.

vijnanabhiksu/vijnanamrta-bhasya/categor.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
vijnanabhiksu/vijnanamrta-bhasya/categor.evidence_note: Discrimination can preserve the body/self distinction while revising which bearer counts as final Self; nonidentity and nondivision are not synonyms.
vijnanabhiksu/vijnanamrta-bhasya/categor.notes: Bhikṣu preserves real individual subjects; his hierarchical reconciliation does not leave every earlier assertion unchanged. Selected primary Sanskrit scan pages visually inspected, with separately identified Yoga comparison.

vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/category-yog.locus: 1.4 and4.22–23; compare Vācaspati’s Tattvavaiśāradī at these sūtras
vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/category-yog.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/category-yog.evidence_note: The reflection accounts allocate consciousness and mental content differently; subsequent explicit self-report is not identical to the initial object-directed episode.
vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/category-yog.notes: Return-image bookkeeping alone does not prove the complete commentators equivalent; later report is not a mandatory infinite regress. Selected1884 Sanskrit scan pages independently inspected; source and commentator voices separated.

sridhara/nyaya-kandali/category-nyaya-se.locus: 1895 edition printed73,83,85–88 (self and memory);323–324 (viśeṣa);278–287 (practice and release)
sridhara/nyaya-kandali/category-nyaya-se.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
sridhara/nyaya-kandali/category-nyaya-se.evidence_note: Persistent self, cognition as a quality, individuating difference and the final condition must be formalized separately; qualitative similarity alone does not identify selves.
sridhara/nyaya-kandali/category-nyaya-se.notes: Selected Śrīdhara account: not a claim that every Nyāya author describes liberation identically. Selected Sanskrit1895 scan inspected; modern research transcription used only with declared scan checks.

utpaladeva/isvara-pratyabhijna-karika/ca.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
utpaladeva/isvara-pratyabhijna-karika/ca.evidence_note: Self-manifestation and reflexive apprehension are distinguished from a merely illuminated inert presentation; recognition and bounded experience must be explained.
utpaladeva/isvara-pratyabhijna-karika/ca.notes: The file’s ipv commentary labels denote the accompanying Vṛtti; do not silently attribute these passages to Abhinavagupta. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

abhinavagupta/tantraloka/category-trika-.locus: Tantrāloka3.1–65 with Jayaratha’s Viveka; especially3.5–9,19,45–65 on selective reception, image support, cognition and presentation without a currently present original
abhinavagupta/tantraloka/category-trika-.verification_scope: Selected source argument and conditional mathematical reconstruction independently reviewed; no complete-work/system certification.
abhinavagupta/tantraloka/category-trika-.evidence_note: An ordinary mirror selectively receives visible form rather than every property; image support, the means of knowing it, registration and efficacy have different roles. Presentations without a currently present external original lead to the larger argument about consciousness’s intrinsic powers.
abhinavagupta/tantraloka/category-trika-.notes: Root and Jayaratha’s explanations remain separate. The mirror example alone does not prove universal manifestation by consciousness. Limited cognition, paśyantī’s differentiated reflection and complete reflexivity must not be identified. The selected fullness/reflection join is conditional on illustrative episode-head assignments. A complete constitutional profile is not current local apprehension or local instantiation of every included property. The two-determination model does not verify the complete tattva taxonomy or reconcile intrinsic-agency doctrines. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/cate.locus: Commentary on extended5–8 block; electronic lines710–738
abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/cate.verification_scope: Selected source argument and conditional mathematical reconstruction independently reviewed; no complete-work/system certification.
abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/cate.evidence_note: Constitutive prerequisites and retention of completed manifestation support a fullness construction in which determinations remain distinct despite complete constitutive inclusion.
abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/cate.notes: The mathematical closure theorem additionally requires explicit compositional inheritance. The local ordered list does not separately enumerate all standard36 tattvas. The selected fullness/reflection join is conditional on illustrative episode-head assignments. A complete constitutional profile is not current local apprehension or local instantiation of every included property. The two-determination model does not verify the complete tattva taxonomy or reconcile intrinsic-agency doctrines. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

devi/devi-gita/category-sakta.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
devi/devi-gita/category-sakta.evidence_note: The Goddess’s power, manifested plurality, knowledge and devotion are articulated within their own textual instruction.
devi/devi-gita/category-sakta.notes: This source cannot be equated with all Śākta or Trika accounts; shared imagery alone does not establish equivalence. Selected GRETIL working Sanskrit witness; source lines and voices retained in reviewed dossier.

madhusudana/bhakti-rasayana/category-mad.locus: First ullāsa with own commentary, electronic PDF3–12 and38–42; root2.46–50, within2.44–60 and3.1–15
madhusudana/bhakti-rasayana/category-mad.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
madhusudana/bhakti-rasayana/category-mad.evidence_note: The developmental account permits increased divine love after specified nondual knowledge; retained realization and occurrent devotional cognition need not be one occurrence-type.
madhusudana/bhakti-rasayana/category-mad.notes: The electronic witness is not a photographic facsimile of its cited1998 print edition; the model is not all eleven stages. Institutional electronic Sanskrit transcription, selected argument visually read; PDF page numbering used.

ramana/upadesa-saram/category-ramana.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
ramana/upadesa-saram/category-ramana.evidence_note: Highest devotion is associated with stable true being; temporary mental suppression differs from lasting correction, and self-vision and divine vision are coordinated.
ramana/upadesa-saram/category-ramana.notes: This is Ramaṇa’s particular account, not a proof that all devotional practices have identical mechanisms. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

ramakrishna/kathamrita/category-ramakris.locus: Kathāmṛta:27October1882 pp84–85; gem/radiance and water/waves pp253–254;22September1883 p269;11March1886 pp1019–1021;14December1884 pp712–714;1March1885 pp748–749;25February1885 pp739–742, institutional Bengali pagination
ramakrishna/kathamrita/category-ramakris.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
ramakrishna/kathamrita/category-ramakris.evidence_note: Brahman and Śakti are described as one reality under inactive and active descriptions; the recorded teaching also distinguishes nondual knowledge from a fuller return to divine manifestation and devotional relationship.
ramakrishna/kathamrita/category-ramakris.notes: Bengali conversation record by M.; not an autograph Sanskrit treatise. The water analogy at p269 names cold/freezing power; wetness in a modern translation is not silently attributed to the Bengali. Postknowledge return is qualified, not a rule requiring every knower to retain a body. Institutional Bengali conversation witnesses, selected connected passages.

vivekananda/complete-works/category-vive.locus: VolIII Bhakti-Yoga, The Philosophy of Ishvara; Para-Bhakti IV The Forms of Love—Manifestation and X The Unity of the Trinity; VolII The Real and the Apparent Man
vivekananda/complete-works/category-vive.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
vivekananda/complete-works/category-vive.evidence_note: Fulfilled love and nondual knowledge are coordinated, with continuing relational expression distinguished from ignorance of identity. Para-Bhakti IV explicitly describes many fulfilled devotees continuing to live for worship.
vivekananda/complete-works/category-vive.notes: Vivekananda’s synthetic argument is not silently assigned to Śaṅkara or Rāmānuja when he quotes them. Continued embodied worship is affirmed for many fulfilled devotees, not imposed as a necessity on every knower. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

aurobindo/life-divine/category-aurobindo.locus: The Life Divine, CWSA21–22: I.III–IV pp27–37;I.X p90;I.XIII pp120–123;II.II pp336–374, especially347–348,351,361–362;II.III pp382–385
aurobindo/life-divine/category-aurobindo.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.
aurobindo/life-divine/category-aurobindo.evidence_note: Valid silent realization need not exhaust reality. Aurobindo argues that determinate manifestation must belong to the infinite’s own power rather than an independent outside, and that its nonbinding possibility still requires an account of the law of manifestation.
aurobindo/life-divine/category-aurobindo.notes: The argument requires more than self-presence: reality of manifestation, absence of an independent outside and the revelatory force of dynamic realization are substantive premises. It neither makes every conceivable form possible nor certifies his reading of every rival school. Official CWSA21–22 English text, selected continuous argument neighborhoods.

ksemaraja/pratyabhijna-hrdaya/category-k.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.

ksemaraja/pratyabhijna-hrdaya/category-k.notes: The feminine noun for consciousness is explicitly free: grammatical gender alone does not impose a universal identity/modality ontology. Selected electronic primary witness; not a critical edition or complete-work certification.

medhananda/infinite-paths-to-infinite-re.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.

gaudapada/mandukya-karika/category-gauda.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.

mandana/brahma-siddhi/category-mandana.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.

suresvara/brhadaranyaka-bhashya-varttika.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.

vidyaranya/jivanmukti-viveka/category-vi.verification_scope: Selected interpretive claim and source chain; no quotation or full-work certification.

ātmābhāsas tu tiṅvācyo dhātvarthaś ca dhiyaḥ kriyā /
ubhayaṃ cāvivekena jānātīty ucyate mṛṣā //

na buddher avabodho 'sti nātmano vidyate kriyā /

shankara/upadesa-sahasri/inspectable-a-s.english_close: The appearance of the self is what the finite verb ending expresses, and the root-meaning is the intellect’s activity. Both, through non-discrimination, are falsely spoken of as “knows.” There is no awareness belonging to the intellect, and no activity exists in the self. shankara/upadesa-sahasri/inspectable-a-s.english_close: People accept a likeness of the face in a mirror, for the face’s reflection is seen in the form of the face. Where there is the appearance of one in another, through non-discrimination of just those two, all people naturally speak of the activity as “knows.” Having superimposed the intellect’s agency, the knower is said to know; likewise, having superimposed consciousness, knowingness is here spoken of as belonging to the intellect. Knowledge is the self’s own nature, eternal light, because of scripture; therefore it is never made by the intellect, by the self, or by another.

shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.original_text: nahyātmāgantukaḥ kasyacit, svayaṃsiddhatvāt / nahyātmātmanaḥ pramāṇamapekṣya sidhyati / tasya hi pratyakṣādīni pramāṇānyaprasiddhaprameyasiddhaya upādīyante / nahyākāśādayaḥ padārdhāḥ pramāṇanirapekṣāḥ svayaṃsiddhāḥ kenacidabhyupagamyante / ātmā tu pramāṇādivyavahārāśrayatvātprāgeva pramāṇādivyavahārātsidhyati / naceddṛśasya nirākaraṇaṃ saṃbhavati / āgantukaṃ hi vastu nirākriyate na svarūpam / ya eva hi nirākartā tadeva tasya svarūpam / nahyagnerauṣṇyamagninā nirākriyate /
shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.english_close: For the self is not adventitious to anyone, being established by itself. For the self is not established by awaiting a means of knowledge about itself. Its means of knowledge, perception and the others, are employed to establish objects of knowledge not already established. For no one accepts things such as space as established by themselves independently of means of knowledge. The self, however, because it is the support of transactions involving means of knowledge and the rest, is established before those transactions. Nor is negation of such [a self] possible. An adventitious thing is negated, not one’s own nature. For whoever is the negator is precisely that one’s own nature. Fire’s heat is not negated by fire.

nanu sthitāyāmapi kartṛtvaśaktau kartṛtvakāryaparihārātpuruṣārthaḥ setsyati / tatparihāraśca nimittaparihārāt / yathāgnerdahanaśaktiyuktasyāpi kāṣṭhaviyogāddahanakāryābhāvāt /

na / nimittānāmapi śaktilakṣaṇena saṃbandhena saṃbaddhānāmatyantaparihārāsaṃbhavāt /

nanu mokṣasādhanavidhānānmokṣaḥ setsyati /

na / sādhanāyattasyānityatvāt / apica nityaśuddhabuddhamuktātmapratipādanānmokṣasiddhirabhimatā / tādṛgātmapratipādanaṃ ca na svābhāvike kartṛtve 'vakalpeta / tasmādupādhidharmādhyāsenaivātmanaḥ kartṛtvaṃ na svābhāvikam /
shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.english_close: [Objection:] Even while the capacity for agency remains, the human goal will be accomplished through avoiding agency’s effect; and avoiding that [effect] comes from avoiding its occasion, just as fire, though endowed with the capacity to burn, has no burning-effect through separation from wood. [Reply:] No, because it is impossible wholly to avoid even the occasions, connected through the relation characterized by capacity. [Objection:] Liberation will be accomplished because its means are prescribed. [Reply:] No, because what depends on means is impermanent. Moreover, liberation is held to be established through teaching the self as eternally pure, aware and free. Teaching such a self would not be possible if agency were intrinsic. Therefore the self’s agency is only through superimposition of properties of limiting conditions, not intrinsic.

na ca dṛśyā dṛṣṭirdraṣṭāraṃ viṣayīkartumutsahate, yatastāmākāṅkṣeta /
na ca svarūpaviṣayākhāṅkṣāsvasyaiva /

shankara/brhadaranyaka-bhashya/inspectab.english_close: Nor is the seeing that is seen capable of making the seer an object, so that one might desire it. Nor is there a desire on the part of oneself concerning one’s own nature as an object. Therefore “it knew only itself” means solely the cessation of superimposition through ignorance, not making the self an object.

shankara/brhadaranyaka-bhashya/inspectab.original_text:
tat sampūrṇamākāśavad vyāpi nirantaraṃ nirupādhikaṃ ca tadevedaṃ sopādhikaṃ nāmarūpasthaṃvyavahārāpannaṃ pūrṇaṃ svena rūpeṇa paramātmanā vyāpyeva nopādhiparicchinnena viśeṣātmanā /
tadidaṃ viśeṣāpannaṃ kāryātmakaṃ brahma pūrṇāt kāraṇātmana udacyata udricyata udgacchatītyetat /
yadyapi kāryātmanodricyate tathāpi yat svarūpaṃ pūrṇatvaṃ paramātmabhāvaṃ tanna jāhāti pūrṇamevodricyate /
shankara/brhadaranyaka-bhashya/inspectab.english_close: That is complete, pervasive like space, without gaps and without limiting conditions. This very [reality], with limiting conditions, situated in name and form, entered into transactions, is complete—pervasive through its own nature as the supreme Self, not through its particular nature delimited by limiting conditions. This Brahman, entered into particularity and having the nature of an effect, rises from the complete having the nature of a cause: rises up, comes forth—this is the meaning. Although it rises as an effect, it does not abandon what is its own nature, completeness, the condition of the supreme Self; it comes forth complete.

shankara/brhadaranyaka-bhashya/inspectab.original_text:
atraike varṇayanti-pūrṇātkāraṇātpūrṇaṃ kāryamudricyate /
udriktaṃ kāryaṃ vartamānakāle 'pi pūrṇameva paramārthavastubhūtaṃ dvaitarūpeṇa /
punaḥ pralayakāle pūrṇasya kāryasya pūrṇatāmādāyā'tmani dhitvā pūrṇamevāvaśiṣyate kāraṇarūpam /
evamutpattisthitipralayeṣu triṣvapi kāleṣu kāryakāraṇayoḥ pūrṇataiva /
sā caikaiva pūrṇatā kāryakāraṇayorbhedena vyapadiśyate /
evaṃ ca dvaitādvaitātmakamekaṃ brahma /
yathā kila samudro jalataraṅgaphenabudbudādyātmaka eva /
yathā ca jalaṃ satyaṃ tadudbhavāśca taraṅgaphelabudbudādayaḥ samudrātmabhūtā evā'virbhāvatirobhāvadharmiṇaḥ paramārthasatyā eva /
evaṃ sarvamidaṃ dvaitaṃ paramārthasatyameva jalataraṅgādisthānīyaṃ samudrajalasthānīyaṃ tu paraṃ brahma /
shankara/brhadaranyaka-bhashya/inspectab.english_close: Here some explain: the complete effect rises from the complete cause. The arisen effect is complete even while present, a thing that is ultimately real in the form of duality. Again, at dissolution, taking the completeness of the complete effect and placing it in oneself, the complete alone remains as cause. Thus in all three times—origination, continuance and dissolution—cause and effect are complete. That completeness is one, designated through the distinction of cause and effect. Thus Brahman is one, with the nature of duality and nonduality. Just as, supposedly, the ocean consists precisely of water, waves, foam, bubbles and the rest; and just as water is real and its arising waves, foam, bubbles and the rest are the ocean itself, possess appearance and disappearance, and are ultimately real: so all this duality is ultimately real, occupying the place of waves and the rest, while highest Brahman occupies the place of the ocean’s water.

na tviha tathā vastuviṣaye dvaitaṃ vā syādadvaitaṃ veti vikalpaḥ sambhavatyapuruṣatantratvādātmavastunaḥ /
virodhācca dvaitādvaitatvayorekasya /
tasmānna suvivakṣiteyaṃ kalpanā /


nanu brahmaṇo dvaitādvaitātmakatve samudrādidṛṣṭāntā vidyante kathamucyate bhavataikasya dvaitādvaitatvaṃ viruddhamiti /
na /
anyaviṣayatvāt /
nityāniravayavavastuviṣayaṃ hi viruddhatvamavocāma dvaitādvaitatvasya na kāryaviṣaye sāvayave /
shankara/brhadaranyaka-bhashya/inspectab.english_close: But here, concerning reality, no option is possible of “it may be duality or it may be nonduality,” because the reality that is the self is not dependent on a person; and because duality and nonduality in one thing contradict. Therefore this conception has not been carefully intended. [Objection:] If Brahman has the nature of duality and nonduality, there are examples such as the ocean; how do you say that duality and nonduality of one thing contradict? [Reply:] No, because [those examples] concern another domain. We said that duality and nonduality contradict concerning an eternal, partless reality, not concerning a composite effect.

nigṛhītasya manaso nirvikalpasya dhīmataḥ  /
pracāraḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ suṣupte 'nyo na tatsamaḥ //

līyate hi suṣupte tan nigṛhītaṃ na līyate  /
tad eva nirbhayaṃ brahma jñānālokaṃ samantataḥ //

ajam anidram asvapnam anāmakam arūpakam  /
sakṛdvibhātaṃ sarvajñaṃ nopacāraḥ kathaṃcana //
gaudapada/mandukya-karika/inspectable-a-.english_close: The course of the restrained, nonconceptual mind of the discerning person is to be understood; in deep sleep it is different, not the same as that. For in deep sleep it subsides; restrained, it does not subside. That very [reality] is fearless Brahman, the light of knowledge all around. Unborn, sleepless, dreamless, nameless, formless, once-for-all manifest, all-knowing: this is in no way a figurative expression.

laye saṃbodhayec cittaṃ vikṣiptaṃ śamayet punaḥ  /
sakaṣāyaṃ (vijānīyāt sama [b:]vijānīyāc chama)prāptaṃ na cālayet //

aniṅganam anābhāsaṃ niṣpannaṃ brahma tat tadā //
gaudapada/mandukya-karika/inspectable-a-.english_close: In subsidence one should awaken the mind; when distracted, quiet it again. One should recognize it as having residual coloring; when it has reached evenness, one should not stir it. One should not savor happiness there; one should become unattached through discernment. One should effortfully unify the mind when, though still, it goes outward. When the mind neither subsides nor is distracted again, then that, unmoving and without appearance, is accomplished Brahman.

Translation follows the first reading recorded in the electronic witness, samaprāpta, attained evenness; the alternative śamaprāpta means attained quiet/tranquillity. mandana-misra/brahma-siddhi/inspectable-.original_text: atha tu vākyāntarāttattvaniṣṭhādadhigate tadviṣayapratyayapravāhavidhānamiṣyate / bhavatu / na kaściddoṣaḥ / tathā ca ‘vijñāya prajñāṃ kurvīta'ityātmatattvavijñānasya siddhatāṃ darśayati / tadapi vā vyarthameva, prāptārthatvāt / sākṣātkaraṇaphalaṃ hi tattadanucintanaṃ dṛṣṭārtham, na tato 'nyatphalamākāṅkṣyate / amṛtatvaṃ hi na svarūpāvirbhāvādanyaditi prāgvarṇitam /
mandana-misra/brahma-siddhi/inspectable-.english_close: But if, when [reality] has been understood from another sentence directed at reality, the prescribing of a stream of cognitions concerning it is desired, let it be: there is no fault. And thus “having understood, one should develop understanding” shows that knowledge of the self’s reality is established. Or that too is useless, because its object is already obtained. For repeated contemplation of that has immediate realization as its result, an observed purpose; no result other than that is sought. For immortality is not different from the manifestation of one’s own nature, as explained before.

vacaspati/bhamati/inspectable-a-vac-dist.original_text: ayamabhisaṃdhiḥ-na vayaṃ pradhānavadavidyāṃ sarvajīveṣvekāmācakṣmahe, yainevamupālamemahi, kintviyaṃ pratijīvaṃ bhidyate / tena yasyaiva jīvasya vidyotpannā tasyaivāvidyāpanīyate na jīvāntarasya, bhinnādhikaraṇayorvidyāvidyayoravirodhāt, tatkutaḥ samastasaṃsārocchedaprasaṅgaḥ /
vacaspati/bhamati/inspectable-a-vac-dist.english_close: This is the intention: we do not declare ignorance to be one in all jīvas like pradhāna, so that we would be reproached in this way; rather it differs for each jīva. Therefore ignorance is removed only for the jīva for whom knowledge has arisen, not for another jīva, because knowledge and ignorance in different loci do not contradict. Whence, then, the consequence that all saṃsāra would be destroyed?

ajñānopahitaṃ bimbacaitanyam īśvaraḥ, antaḥkaraṇatatsaṃskārāvacchinnājñānapratibimbitaṃ caitanyaṃ jīva iti vivaraṇakārāḥ / ajñānapratibimbitaṃ caitanyam īśvaraḥ, buddhipratibimbitaṃ caitanyaṃ jīvaḥ, ajñānopahitaṃ tu bimbacaitanyaṃ śuddham iti saṅkṣepaśārīrakakārāḥ / anayoś ca pakṣayoḥ buddhibhedāj jīvanānātvam /

ajñānaviṣayībhūtaṃ caitanyam īśvaraḥ, ajñānāśrayībhūtaṃ ca jīva iti vācaspatimiśrāḥ / asmiṃś ca pakṣe ajñānanānātvāj jīvanānātvam /
madhusudana/siddhanta-bindu/inspectable-.english_close: “The prototype-consciousness conditioned by ignorance is Īśvara; consciousness reflected in ignorance delimited by the inner instrument and its dispositions is jīva”: thus the authors of the Vivaraṇa. “Consciousness reflected in ignorance is Īśvara; consciousness reflected in intellect is jīva; prototype-consciousness conditioned by ignorance is pure”: thus the author of the Saṃkṣepaśārīraka. In these two positions the plurality of jīvas follows from difference of intellects. “Consciousness made the object of ignorance is Īśvara, and made its locus is jīva”: thus Vācaspati Miśra. In this position plurality of jīvas follows from plurality of ignorance.

advitīyātmatattvaṃ hi pradhānaṃ phalavattvād ajñātatvāc ca prameyaṃ śāstrasya / jīveśvaravibhāgādikalpanās tu puruṣabuddhimātraprabhavā api śāstreṇānūdyante, tattvajñānopayogitvāt / phalavat sannidhāv aphalaṃ tadaṅgam iti nyāyāt bhramasiddhasyāpi śrutyānuvādasambhavāt / 

śrutitātparyaviṣayībhūtārthaviruddhatvaṃ ca heyam eveti śataśa udghoṣitam asmābhiḥ /
madhusudana/siddhanta-bindu/inspectable-.english_close: For the nondual reality of the self is scripture’s principal object of knowledge, because it is fruitful and unknown. Conceptions such as division into jīva and Īśvara, although arising merely from human understanding, are restated by scripture because they are useful for knowledge of reality: according to the rule that what is without its own fruit, in proximity to what has a fruit, is subordinate to it, and because scripture can restate even what is established through error. We have proclaimed hundreds of times that contradiction of the meaning intended by scripture must indeed be rejected.

ekatvasaṅkhyāyogi ekam / tad apekṣābuddhijanyadvitvasaṅkhyāyogi dvitīyam / tata ekābhāve dvitīyaṃ kutaḥ syāt / dvitīyaṃ ca tṛtīyādīnām apy upalakṣaṇam / nanu, "ekam evādvitīyam" (chu vi.2.1.) iti śrutyā ekatvaṃ pratipādyate / na, ity āha -- na vā kevalatvam iti / kevalam ekatvaṃ, tasyāvidyakatvāt / yady ātmana ekatvaṃ śrutyā na pratipādyate, tarhi pratyakṣādipramāṇavaśād anekatvaṃ syād iti cet, na, ity āha -- na cākevalatvam iti / akevalatvam anekatvaṃ, "neha nānāsti kiñcana" (bau iv.4.19.), "ekam evādvitīyam" (chu vi.2.1.), "athāta ādeśo neti neti" (bau ii.3.6.) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ / 

sarvatra hetum āha -- advaitakatvād iti / dvidhā itaṃ dvītaṃ tasya bhāvo dvaitam / tad uktaṃ vārtike "dvidhetaṃ dvītam ity āhus tadbhāvo dvaitam ucyate" (baubhv iv.3.1807.) iti / na vidyate dvaitaṃ dvidhābhāvo yatra tad advaitam ity akṣarārthaḥ / "salila eko dṛṣṭādvaitaḥ" (bau iv.3.32.) itiśruteḥ /
madhusudana/siddhanta-bindu/inspectable-.english_close: “One” is what possesses the number one. “Second” is what possesses the number two generated by a cognition of reference to that [one]. Therefore, when there is no one, whence a second? “Second” also stands for third and the rest. [Objection:] Scripture, “one alone, without a second,” teaches oneness. [Reply:] No; he says “nor sole-ness.” Sole-ness is oneness, because that is due to ignorance. [Objection:] If the self’s oneness is not taught by scripture, plurality would follow through perception and other means of knowledge. [Reply:] No; he says “nor non-sole-ness.” Non-sole-ness is plurality, [excluded] by scriptural passages including “there is no plurality here whatsoever,” “one alone, without a second,” and “not this, not this.” He gives the reason throughout: “because of nonduality.” What has gone twofold is dvīta; its condition is duality. The Vārttika says: “They call what has gone twofold dvīta; its condition is called duality.” Where duality, the condition of being twofold, does not exist, that is advaita: this is the literal meaning, because scripture says “one seer like water, nondual.”

ekatvasaṅkhyāyogi ekam / tad apekṣābuddhijanyadvitvasaṅkhyāyogi dvitīyam / tata ekābhāve dvitīyaṃ kutaḥ syāt / dvitīyaṃ ca tṛtīyādīnām apy upalakṣaṇam / nanu, "ekam evādvitīyam" (chu vi.2.1.) iti śrutyā ekatvaṃ pratipādyate / na, ity āha -- na vā kevalatvam iti / kevalam ekatvaṃ, tasyāvidyakatvāt / yady ātmana ekatvaṃ śrutyā na pratipādyate, tarhi pratyakṣādipramāṇavaśād anekatvaṃ syād iti cet, na, ity āha -- na cākevalatvam iti / akevalatvam anekatvaṃ, "neha nānāsti kiñcana" (bau iv.4.19.), "ekam evādvitīyam" (chu vi.2.1.), "athāta ādeśo neti neti" (bau ii.3.6.) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ / 

sarvatra hetum āha -- advaitakatvād iti / dvidhā itaṃ dvītaṃ tasya bhāvo dvaitam / tad uktaṃ vārtike "dvidhetaṃ dvītam ity āhus tadbhāvo dvaitam ucyate" (baubhv iv.3.1807.) iti / na vidyate dvaitaṃ dvidhābhāvo yatra tad advaitam ity akṣarārthaḥ / "salila eko dṛṣṭādvaitaḥ" (bau iv.3.32.) itiśruteḥ /

madhusudana/siddhanta-bindu/inspectable-.original_text: atha vā mūlājñānasyaivāvasthājñānāni ghaṭādiviṣayāvaraṇāni / ajñānasya prāgabhāvasthānīyatvena yāvanti jñānāni tāvanty ajñānānīty abhyupagamāt ekena ca jñānenaikājñānasyaiva nāśāt, ghaṭādijñānenāvaraṇanāśe 'pi na kācid anupapattiḥ /
madhusudana/siddhanta-bindu/inspectable-.english_close: Or else the particular ignorance-states of root ignorance itself are the coverings of objects such as pots. Because ignorance occupies the place of prior absence, it is accepted that there are as many ignorances as knowledges; and because one knowledge destroys only one ignorance, even when a pot-cognition destroys covering there is no inconsistency.
