suresvara/brhadaranyaka-varttika/inspect.original_text:
pramopajāyate tāvadahaṃ brahmetyalaukikī | tattvamasyādivākyebhyaḥ śravaṇātsamanantaram || 167 ||
nāpyarthe'tīndriye siddhe mānaṃ liṅgādyapekṣate | yogipratyakṣamānaṃ vā tayoraviṣayatvataḥ || 170 ||
netītyasthūlamityādivākyādyo'rtho'vagamyate | yogipratyakṣagamyo'yaṃ na tatpratyaktvahetutaḥ || 171 ||
suresvara/brhadaranyaka-varttika/inspect.english_close: First, the extraordinary knowledge “I am Brahman” arises from sentences such as “you are that,” immediately upon hearing. Nor does a means of knowledge concerning an established supersensible reality await an inferential mark or the like, or a means of knowledge consisting in yogic perception, because [that reality] is not their object. The meaning understood from sentences such as “not this” and “not gross” is not accessible to yogic perception, because it is inward.

suresvara/brhadaranyaka-varttika/inspect.original_text:
aparāyattabodho'tra nididhyāsanamucyate | pūrvayoravadhitvena tadupanyāsa iṣyate || 217 ||
śravaṇādikriyā tāvatkartavyeha prayatnataḥ | yāvadyathoktaṃ vijñānamāvirbhavati bhāsvaram || 218 ||
dhyānāśaṅkānivṛttyarthaṃ vijñāneneti bhaṇyate | nididhyāsanaśabdena dhyānamāśaṅkyate yataḥ || 233 ||
vijñānotpattihetutvaṃ dhyānādeḥ prāgavādiṣam | svārthameva tu vijñānaṃ muktimātraphalaṃ smṛtam || 234 ||
suresvara/brhadaranyaka-varttika/inspect.english_close: Here understanding not dependent on another is called nididhyāsana; its introduction is intended as the culmination of the preceding two. The activity of hearing and the rest must be performed here with effort until the knowledge described becomes luminously manifest. “Through knowledge” is said to remove the suspicion of meditation, because meditation is suspected from the word nididhyāsana. I previously stated that meditation and the rest cause the arising of knowledge; knowledge itself is for its own purpose, remembered as having liberation alone as its fruit.

padmapada/pancapadika/inspectable-a-pad-.original_text: mithyā ca tadajñānaṃ ca mithyājñānam | mithyeti anirvacanīyatā ucyate | ajñānamiti ca jaḍātmikā avidyāśaktiḥ jñānaparyudāsena ucyate | tannimittaḥ tadupādānaḥ ityarthaḥ ||
padmapada/pancapadika/inspectable-a-pad-.english_close: It is both mithyā and ignorance: mithyājñāna. By mithyā indeterminability is stated. By ajñāna an insentient ignorance-power is stated through exclusion of knowledge. “Having that as its occasion” means “having that as its material source.”

padmapada/pancapadika/inspectable-a-pad-.original_text: atha śuktereva doṣanimitto rajatarūpaḥ pariṇāma ucyate, etadapyasāram ; na hi kṣīrapariṇāme dadhani ‘nedaṃ dadhi’ iti bādho dṛṣṭaḥ ; nāpi kṣīramidam iti pratītiḥ, iha tu tadubhayaṃ dṛśyate | kiñca rajatarūpeṇa cet pariṇatā śuktiḥ, kṣīramiva dadhirūpeṇa, tadā doṣāpagame'pi tathaiva avatiṣṭheta |
padmapada/pancapadika/inspectable-a-pad-.english_close: If a transformation of the shell into silver-form occasioned by a defect is asserted, this too is without substance. For in curd, the transformation of milk, cancellation “this is not curd” is not seen; nor the cognition “this is milk.” Here, however, both are seen. Moreover, if the shell transformed into silver-form like milk into curd-form, even upon disappearance of the defect it would remain just so.

saccidanandendra/mulavidya-nirasa/inspec.original_text: no khalu svabhāvo'yamātmano yadadhyāsavirodhyākāreṇa bhāsamānatvam, kiṃ tu bhāsamānatvameva tasya svabhāvaḥ | adhyāsanirodhakatvaṃ tu pramāṇotpannajñānakṛtyam |

shankara/chandogya-bhashya/inspectable-a.original_text:
kathaṃ mṛtpiṇḍe kāraṇe vijñāte kāryamanyadvijñātaṃ syāt /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
kāraṇenānanyatvātkāryasya /
yanmanyase 'nyasminvijñāte 'nyanna jñāyata iti /
satyamevaṃ syāt /
yadyanyatkāraṇātkāryaṃ syānna tvevamanyatkāraṇātkāryam /
kathaṃ tarhidaṃ loka idaṃ kāraṇamayasya vikāra iti /

śṛṇu /
vācā'rambhaṇaṃ vāgārambhaṇaṃ vāgālambanamityetat /
ko 'sau vikāro nāmadheyaṃ nāmaiva nāmadheyaṃ svārthe dheyapratyayaḥ /
vāgālambanamātraṃ nāmaiva kevalaṃ na vikāro nāma vastvasti paramārthato mṛttiketyeva tu mṛttiketyeva tu mṛttikaiva satyaṃ vastvasti //4 //
shankara/chandogya-bhashya/inspectable-a.english_close: [Objection:] How, when the lump of clay, the cause, is known, would another thing, the effect, be known? [Reply:] This is no fault, because the effect is not other than the cause. You think that when one thing is known another is not known. That would indeed be so if the effect were other than the cause; but the effect is not thus other than the cause. [Objection:] How then [does one say] in the world, “this is the cause; this is its modification”? [Reply:] Listen. “Having speech as commencement” means having speech as commencement, having speech as support. What is that modification? A name: nāmadheya is simply nāman, the suffix dheya being in its own meaning. It is only a name supported by speech; there is no thing called modification ultimately. Clay alone, clay alone—clay alone exists as the real thing.
shankara/chandogya-bhashya/inspectable-a.notes: Objection/reply in Śaṅkara’s bhāṣya Local final sentence duplicates mṛttiketyeva tu; retained as witness repetition. The interpretation does not depend on that duplication.

tathā ca yena sambandhaviśeṣeṇa yena cāvacchedakaviśeṣeṇa yadadhikaraṇatāpratītiryatra bhavitumarhati, tenaiva sambandhaviśeṣeṇa tenaiva cāvacchedakaviśeṣeṇa tadadhikaraṇakātyantābhāvapratiyogitvaṃ tasya mithyātvamiti paryavasite kva siddhasādhanam |
madhusudana/advaitasiddhi/inspectable-a-.english_close: Because the word “apprehended” indicates being the counterpositive of absolute absence in that [locus] in precisely the form in which it is apprehended as the locus of that [thing]. That form is a particular relation and a particular delimiter. For the ground’s being the locus of a pot is not apprehended without a particular relation, nor the tree’s being the locus of contact with a monkey without a particular delimiter. Thus, when the definition comes to this—its falsity is being the counterpositive of absolute absence located there through precisely that particular relation and precisely that particular delimiter through which the cognition of that locushood can occur there—where is the proving of what is already established?

na, svarūpa-sādhana-phalādhikāri-vailakṣaṇyād bhakti-brahma-vidyayoḥ | dravī-bhāva-pūrvikā hi manaso bhagavad-ākāratā savikalpaka-vṛtti-rūpā bhaktiḥ |
dravī-bhāvānupetādvitīyātma-mātra-gocarā nirvikalpaka-mano-vṛttir brahma-vidyā | bhagavad-guṇa-garima-granthana-rūpa-grantha-śravaṇaṃ bhakti-sādhanam | tat tvam asy ādi vedānta-mahā-vākyaṃ brahma-vidyā-sādhanam | bhagavad-viṣayaka-prema-prakarṣo bhakti-phalam | sarvānartha-mūlājñāna-nivṛttir brahma-vidyā-phalam |
madhusudana/bhakti-rasayana/inspectable-.english_close: No, because devotion and Brahman-knowledge differ in nature, means, fruit and qualified recipient. Devotion is the mind’s taking the form of the Lord, preceded by melting, in the form of a determinate modification. Brahman-knowledge is a nondeterminate mental modification, without melting, whose domain is solely the nondual self. Hearing works that arrange the greatness of the Lord’s qualities is the means of devotion. A great Vedānta sentence such as “you are that” is the means of Brahman-knowledge. Intensification of love directed to the Lord is devotion’s fruit; cessation of ignorance, the root of all misfortune, is Brahman-knowledge’s fruit.

śuddha-sattvodbhavāpy evaṃ sādhakeṣv asmad-ādiṣu |
dṛṣṭa-mātra-phalā sā tu siddheṣu sanakādiṣu ||46||
dṛṣṭādṛṣṭa-phalā bhaktiḥ sukha-vyakter vidher api |
nidāgha-dūna-dehasya gaṅgā-snāna-kriyā yathā ||47||
rajas tamo’bhibhūtasya dṛṣṭāṃśaḥ pratibadhyate |
śītavātāturasyeva nādṛṣṭāṃśas tu hīyate ||48||
tathaiva jīvan-muktānām adṛṣṭāṃśo na vidyate |
snātvā bhuktavatāṃ bhūyo gaṅgāyāṃ krīḍatāṃ yathā ||49||
vartamāna-tanu-prāpyaṃ phalaṃ dṛṣṭam udāhṛtam |
bhāvi-dehopabhogyaṃ yat tad adṛṣṭam udīritam ||50||
madhusudana/bhakti-rasayana/inspectable-.english_close: Even devotion born of pure sattva is thus [of both fruits] in practitioners such as ourselves; but in accomplished ones such as Sanaka it has only the seen fruit. Devotion has seen and unseen fruits, because of manifestation of happiness and also prescription, like bathing in the Ganges for one whose body is tormented by summer heat. In one overcome by rajas and tamas, the seen portion is obstructed, as for one afflicted by cold wind; the unseen portion is not lost. In the same way, for those liberated while living there is no unseen portion, as for those who, having bathed and eaten, play again in the Ganges. The fruit attainable in the present body is called seen; that to be enjoyed in a future body is called unseen.

atha jīvanmuktisādhanaṃ nirūpayāmaḥ | tattvajñānamanonāśavāsanākṣayāstatsādhanam |

viveko nāma vibhajyaniścayaḥ - tattvajñānasya śravaṇādikaṃ sādhanam, manonāśasya yogaḥ, vāsanākṣayasya pratikūlavāsanotpādanamiti |
vidyaranya/jivanmukti-viveka/inspectable.english_close: Now we explain the means of liberation while living. Knowledge of reality, dissolution of mind and exhaustion of dispositions are its means. Discernment is a determination by distinguishing: hearing and the rest are the means of knowledge of reality; yoga of dissolution of mind; producing contrary dispositions of exhaustion of dispositions.

shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.original_text:
nanu mṛdādidṛṣṭāntapraṇayanātpariṇāmavadbrahma śāstrasyābhimatamiti gamyate / pariṇāmino hi mṛdādayor'thā loke samadhigatā iti /

netyucyate / 'sa vā eṣa mahājana ātmājaro 'maro 'mṛto 'bhayo brahma' (bṛ. 4.4.25) 'sa eṣa neti netyātmā' (bṛ. 3.9.23), 'asthūlamanaṇu' (bṛ. 3.8.8) ityādyābhyaḥ sarvavikriyāpratiṣedhaśrutibhyo brahmaṇaḥ kūṭasthatvāvagamāt / nahyekasya brahmaṇaḥ pariṇāmadharmatvaṃ tadrahitatvaṃ ca śkyaṃ pratipattum /
shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.english_close: [Objection:] From the introduction of examples such as clay, Brahman possessing transformation is understood to be intended by scripture; for things such as clay are known in the world as transforming. [Reply:] No: Brahman’s invariance is understood from scriptural denials of all modification, such as “this great unborn self, unaging, deathless, immortal, fearless, Brahman,” “this self is not this, not this,” and “not gross, not minute.” For transformation and its absence cannot be understood of the one Brahman.

Stored electronic quotation preserves the defect explicitly. Electronic śkyaṃ also preserved.

shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.original_text: tatraitatsiddhaṃ bhavati- brahmaprakaraṇe sarvadharmaviśeṣarahitabrahmadarśanādeva phalasiddhau satyāṃ yattatrāphalaṃ śrūyate brahmaṇo jagadākārapariṇāmitvādi tadbrahmadarśanopāyatvenaiva viniyujyate, phalavatsaṃnidhāvaphalaṃ tadaṅgamitivat / natu svatantraṃ phalāya kalpyata iti /
shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.english_close: This is established there: in the discussion of Brahman, since the fruit is accomplished only through seeing Brahman devoid of every particular property, whatever fruitless [teaching] is heard there—Brahman’s transformation into the form of the world and the like—is applied only as a means to seeing Brahman, according to “what is fruitless in proximity to what bears fruit is its subordinate.” It is not imagined as independently for a fruit.

shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.original_text:
sarvajñasyeśvarasyātmabhūta ivāvidyākalpite nāmarūpe tattvānyatvābhyāmanirvacanīye saṃsāraprapañcabījabhūte sarvajñasyeśvarasya māyāśaktiḥ prakṛtiriti ca śrutismṛtyorabhilapyete / 

tadevamavidyātmakopādhiparicchedāpekṣameveśvarasyeśvaratvaṃ sarvajñatvaṃ sarvaśaktitvaṃ ca na paramārthato vidyāyāpāstasarvopādhisvarūpa ātmanīśitrīśitavyasarvajñatvādivyavahāra upapadyate /
shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.english_close: Name and form, imagined through ignorance as though the very self of the omniscient Lord, indefinable as that or other than that, the seeds of the saṃsāric manifold, are called in śruti and smṛti the omniscient Lord’s māyā-power and prakṛti. Thus the Lord’s lordship, omniscience and omnipotence depend precisely on delimitation by ignorance-natured limiting conditions; ultimately, in the self whose nature is stripped of every limiting condition by knowledge, transactions of ruler and ruled, omniscience and the rest do not fit.

shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.original_text: śaktiśca kāraṇasya kāryaniyamārthā kalpamānā nānyāsatī vā kāryaṃ niyacchet / asattvāviśeṣādanyatvāviśeṣācca / tasmātkāraṇasyātmabhūtā śaktiḥ śakteścātmabhūtaṃ kāryam /
shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.english_close: And a power of the cause posited to account for restriction of the effect could not restrict the effect if it were other [than the cause] or nonexistent, because there would be no difference in nonexistence or in otherness. Therefore the power is the cause’s own nature, and the effect is the power’s own nature.

shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.original_text: atrocyate- na svapnādipratyayavajjāgratpratyayā bhavitumarhanti / kasmāt / vaidharmyāt / vaidharmyaṃ hi bhavati svapnajāgaritayoḥ / kiṃ punarvaidharmyam / bādhābādhāviti brūmaḥ / bādhyate hi svapnopalabdhaṃ vastu pratibuddhasya mithyā mayopalabdho mahājanasamāgama iti, nahyasti mama mahājanasamāgamo nidrālagnaṃ tu me mano babhūva tenaiṣā bhrāntirudbabhūveti / evaṃ māyādiṣvapi bhavati yatāvidhaṃ bādhaḥ / naivaṃ jāgaritopalabdhaṃ vastu stambhādikaṃ kasyāñcidapyavasthāyāṃ bādhyate /
shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.english_close: Here it is said: waking cognitions cannot be like dream cognitions. Why? Because of difference. There is indeed a difference between dream and waking. What difference? We say: cancellation and non-cancellation. For what is apprehended in dream is cancelled for the awakened person: “I falsely apprehended a gathering of many people; there is no such gathering for me; my mind was attached to sleep, and so this error arose.” Likewise in magic and the rest cancellation occurs as appropriate. A thing apprehended in waking, such as a post, is not cancelled in any state in this way.
shankara/brahma-sutra-bhasya/inspectable.notes: Śaṅkara’s reply to external-object denial The scope of “in any state” and its relation to ultimate cancellation require explicit contextual interpretation; the dossier does not assert that the tension disappears by notation.

padmapada/pancapadika/inspectable-a-pad-.original_text: ‘adhyasya’ ‘mithunīkṛtya’ iti ca ktvāpratyayaḥ, na pūrvakālatvamanyatvaṃ ca lokavyavahārādaṅgīkṛtya prayuktaḥ ; bhuktvā vrajatītivat kriyāntarānupādānāt | ‘adhyasya naisargiko'yaṃ lokavyavahāraḥ’ iti svarūpamātraparyavasānāt | upasaṃhāre ca ‘evamayamanādirananto naisargiko'dhyāsaḥ’ iti tāvanmātropasaṃhārāt ||
padmapada/pancapadika/inspectable-a-pad-.english_close: And the ktvā suffix in “having superimposed” and “having coupled” is not used accepting temporal priority and otherness from worldly usage, since no other action is introduced as in “having eaten, he goes”; because “having superimposed, this natural worldly transaction” culminates only in [its] nature, and because in the conclusion, “thus this beginningless, endless, natural superimposition,” only that much is concluded.

vidyaranya/jivanmukti-viveka/inspectable.english_close: There is no weakening of knowledge once it has arisen, because there is no cancelling means of knowledge and no cause for the re-arising of ignorance that has ceased. Exhaustion of dispositions and dissolution of mind, however, because firm practice is absent and because they are obstructed from time to time by already-begun karma that gives experience, suddenly cease like a lamp in a windy place.

The preceding kṛtopāsti case has firm attainments and ensuing liberation while living without this further effort.

iyam ca pañcamī bhūmikā bhakteḥ svarūpam | etasyā eva paripāka-viśeṣād anyāḥ ṣaḍ-bhūmikāḥ phala-bhūtāḥ |

madhusudana/bhakti-rasayana/inspectable-.english_close: This fifth stage is devotion’s own nature. From its particular maturation the other six stages are fruits. Then comes realization of one’s own nature: immediate realization of the inward self’s nature as distinct from the pair of gross and subtle bodies is the sixth stage. Otherwise, through distraction by body, senses and the rest, even affection that has arisen could not be sustained.

vidyaranya/jivanmukti-viveka/inspectable.original_text:
pradīpajvālāsantānavadvṛttisantānarūpeṇa pariṇamamānamantaḥkaraṇadravyaṃ mananātmakatvānmana ityucyate | tasya nāśo nāma vṛttirūpapariṇāmaṃ parityajya niruddhatvākāreṇa pariṇāmaḥ|

pūrvāparaparāmarśamantareṇa sahasotpadyamānasya krodhādivṛttiviśeṣasya hetuścittagataḥ saṃskāro vāsanā, pūrvapūrvābhyāsena citte vāsyamānatvāt |
tasyāśca vāsanāyāḥ kṣayo nāma vivekajanyāyāṃ śāntidāntyādiśuddhavāsanāyāṃ dṛḍhāyāṃ satyapi bāhyanimitte krodhādyanutpattiḥ |
vidyaranya/jivanmukti-viveka/inspectable.english_close:
The substance of the internal organ, transforming in the form of a succession of modifications like a succession of lamp flames, is called mind because its nature is thinking. Its dissolution means transformation in the form of restraint, having abandoned transformation in the form of modifications.

A disposition is the impression in the mind that causes a particular modification such as anger to arise suddenly without consideration of what precedes and follows, because it has been instilled in the mind through repeated earlier practice. Exhaustion of that disposition means the nonarising of anger and the like even when an external occasion is present, once the pure disposition of tranquility, restraint and the like, born of discrimination, is firm.
vidyaranya/jivanmukti-viveka/inspectable.notes: Author’s own teaching Two separated author passages. The intervening Yoga3.9 citation and gloss are not included in this selection.

upanishads/brhadaranyaka/inspectable-a-u.english_close: That is full; this is full. From the full, the full arises. Having taken the full of the full, the full alone remains.

upanishads/brhadaranyaka/inspectable-a-u.notes: Root mantra, distinct from Śaṅkara’s subsequent gloss The complete two-line fullness mantra is quoted, not the complete prose paragraph5.1.1 or a composite invocation with added śānti lines. Pūrṇasya is genitive; the deliberately literal of-the-full rendering avoids silently deciding whether ādāya is subtraction. Subsequent Śaṅkara explains taking through knowledge/appropriation of one’s complete nature.

madhusudana/bhakti-rasayana/inspectable-.english_close: For [what is required] for identity of the effect is identity of the complete causal assemblage, not merely identity of a cause, because [otherwise] overextension follows. Thus devotion and Brahman-knowledge too, like heaven and the desire to know, will lack a fruit-and-means relation and will be attainable through similar means.

madhusudana/bhakti-rasayana/inspectable-.notes: Madhusūdana’s own reply, not the immediately following objection Two connected closing sentences of a longer complete paragraph visually read. The preceding ritual analogy distinguishes heaven and desire-to-know as different results from overlapping practices. Do not infer complete absence of every causal relation at every stage; later stages state particular developmental relations. Bracketed what-is-required exposes the English ellipsis of the compressed Sanskrit.

umasvati-pujyapada/tattvarthasutra-sarva.original_text: utpādavyayadhrauvyayuktaṃ sat || […] cetanasyācetanasya vā dravyasya svāṃ jātim ajahata ubhayanimittavaśād bhāvāntarāvāptir utpādanam utpādaḥ mṛtpiṇḍasya ghaṭaparyāyavat. tathā pūrvabhāvavigamanaṃ vyayaḥ. yathā ghaṭotpattau piṇḍākṛte. anādipāriṇāmikasvabhāvena vyayodayābhāvād dhruvati sthirībhavatīti dhruvaḥ. dhruvasya bhāvaḥ karma vā dhrauvyam. yathā mṛtpiṇḍaghaṭādyavasthāsu mṛdādyanvayaḥ.
umasvati-pujyapada/tattvarthasutra-sarva.english_close: The real is endowed with arising, passing away and permanence. […] Arising is the attainment of another condition, through both kinds of conditions, by a conscious or unconscious substance without abandoning its own kind—as a lump of clay attains the pot-mode. Likewise, passing away is departure of the preceding condition, as [the loss] of lump-shape when a pot arises. What persists, becomes stable, through absence of loss or arising in its beginningless constitutive nature is enduring; endurance is its condition or activity—as clay continues through lump, pot and other states.

pujyapada/sarvartha-siddhi/inspectable-j.original_text: etad uktaṃ bhavati — utpādādīni dravyasya lakṣaṇāni. dravyaṃ lakṣyam. tatra paryāyārthikanayāpekṣayā parasparato dravyāc cārthāntarabhāvaḥ. dravyārthikanayāpekṣayā vyatirekeṇānupalabdher anarthāntarabhāvaḥ. iti lakṣyalakṣaṇabhāvasiddhiḥ.
pujyapada/sarvartha-siddhi/inspectable-j.english_close: What has been said is this: arising and the rest are characteristics of substance; substance is what is characterized. Here, relative to the standpoint directed at modes, there is distinctness from one another and from substance. Relative to the standpoint directed at substance, there is nondistinctness, because they are not apprehended separately. Thus the relation of characterized and characteristic is established.

pujyapada/sarvartha-siddhi/inspectable-j.english_close: The thing formerly seen is recognized as “this is that very thing” because it occurs again with precisely that nature. If there were complete destruction, or only an entirely new appearance, recollection would not be possible; worldly transactions dependent on it would be contradicted. […] But that [eternity] is to be understood in a qualified way. With eternity in every respect, because there would be no becoming otherwise, the causal process of transmigration and its cessation would be contradicted.

umasvati-pujyapada/tattvarthasutra-sarva.english_close: Perfect knowledge [arises] from the destruction of delusion and from the destruction of the knowledge- and perception-obscuring and obstructive [karmas]. […] True [that a shorter wording was possible]; but the formulation in separate clauses is made to teach the order of destruction. Having first brought delusion to destruction, and having obtained the designation “passions destroyed” for less than a muhūrta, one then destroys together the knowledge- and perception-obscuring and obstructive [karmas] and attains perfect knowledge. Their destruction is the cause of perfect knowledge’s arising; therefore the case ending indicating a cause was employed.

umasvati-pujyapada/tattvarthasutra-sarva.english_close: Liberation is complete release from all karma, through absence of the causes of bondage and through shedding [karma]. […] [Pūjyapāda:] This rule [of cessation] applies to whatever is other than perfect rightness, knowledge, perception and the state of a perfected being. [Objection:] If only four remain, would not unlimited power and so forth cease? [Reply:] This is no fault: unlimited power and so forth are not separate [exceptions], because they are inseparable from knowledge and perception; for the activity of unlimited cognition is absent in one lacking unlimited capacity, and happiness consists of knowledge.

pujyapada/sarvartha-siddhi/inspectable-j.english_close: [Objection:] These released ones have only discourse about past differences, since the causes of differences of destination, birth-class and so forth are absent. [Reply:] There is also difference in a certain respect. Why? […] As regards time: at what time is perfection? With reference to the standpoint of the present, one attaining perfection in a single instant becomes perfected. With reference to the standpoint that describes the past, as regards birth, without further specification, one born in an ascending or descending [time-cycle] attains perfection.

siddharsiganin/nyayavatara-vivrti/inspec.original_text: kartā bhoktā iti viśeṣaṇa-dvayena sāṃkhya-mataṃ vikuṭṭayati, kartā san bhoktāpīti kākvopanyāsād, akartur bhogānupapatter, bhuji-kriyā-nirvartana-samarthasyaiva bhoktṛtvāt. japā-kusumādi-sannidhāna-vaśāt sphaṭike raktatādi-vyapadeśavad akartur api prakṛty-upadhāna-vaśāt sukha-duḥkhādi-bhoga-vyapadeśo yuktas; tathā hi: prakṛti-vikāra-darpaṇākāra-buddhi-saṅkrāntānāṃ sukha-duḥkhādy-ātmakānām arthānāṃ puruṣaḥ sannidhāna-mātreṇa bhojako vyapadiśyate, "buddhy-adhyavasitam arthaṃ puruṣaś cetayata" iti-vacanād iti cen, na, kathañcit sakriyākatā-vyatirekeṇa prakṛty-upadhāne 'py anyathātvānupapatter, apracyuta-prācīna-rūpasya vyapadeśānarhatvāt, tat-pracyave ca prāktana-rūpa-tyāgenottara-rūpādhyāsitayā sakriyatvam āpatatīti-nyāyāt; sphaṭika-dṛṣṭānte 'pi japā-kusumādi-sannidhānād andhopalādau raktatānāvir-bhavantī tatra punar āvir-bhavantī tasya tathā-vidhaṃ pariṇāmaṃ lakṣayaty. […] tan nākriyasya bhoktṛtopapadyata iti.
siddharsiganin/nyayavatara-vivrti/inspec.english_close: By the two qualifications “agent” and “experiencer” he attacks the Sāṅkhya view: the emphatic construction is “being an agent, he is also an experiencer,” since experience is impossible for a nonagent, and only one able to perform the act of experiencing is an experiencer. [Objection:] Just as redness and so on are predicated of crystal through the proximity of a hibiscus flower and the like, pleasure, pain and other experience may properly be predicated of an inactive [self] through the adjunct of primordial nature. For the person, merely by proximity, is called the enjoyer of objects consisting of pleasure, pain and so forth that have entered the mirror-like intellect, a transformation of primordial nature; as it is said, “The person is conscious of the object determined by intellect.” [Reply:] No. Without activity in some respect, becoming otherwise would be impossible even with primordial nature as an adjunct. What has not departed from its earlier form is not fit for that predication; if it does depart, activity follows from abandoning the earlier form and assuming the later. Even in the crystal example, redness that fails to appear in an opaque stone and the like through the hibiscus flower’s proximity, but does appear there [in the crystal], indicates such a transformation of it. […] Thus being an experiencer does not fit the inactive.

nagarjuna-candrakirti/mulamadhyamakakari.english_close: [Objection:] But that yogin who thus becomes free of “mine” and “I” does exist. Given his existence, self and aggregates are established. [Reply:] It is not so. For: even the one who is free of “mine” and “I” is not found. Whoever sees one free of “mine” and “I” does not see.

nagarjuna-candrakirti/mulamadhyamakakari.english_close: Liberation comes from the ending of action and afflictions; action and afflictions arise from conceptual construction; those [constructions] from proliferation, while proliferation ceases in emptiness. […] From the departure of proliferation comes cessation of conceptual construction; from cessation of conceptual construction, cessation of all action and afflictions; and from cessation of action and afflictions, cessation of birth.

nagarjuna-candrakirti/mulamadhyamakakari.english_close: [Nāgārjuna:] “Self” has also been designated, and “nonself” also taught; the Buddhas have also taught that there is neither any self nor any nonself. […] [Candrakīrti:] To turn away from unwholesomeness and so forth those less advanced pupils who perform unwholesome actions, the Blessed Buddhas in some cases also designated “self,” establishing it in the world. […] For those intermediate pupils, to loosen fixation on the view of a real personal identity and to generate desire for nirvāṇa, […] “nonself” too was taught. […] For those advanced pupils whose attachment to self has gone […] [the neither-self-nor-nonself teaching quoted again in the intervening text]. […] For just as the view of self is not reality, so the view of nonself that opposes it is itself not reality.

nagarjuna-candrakirti/mulamadhyamakakari.original_text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ śūnyatāṃ tāṃ pracakṣmahe / sā prajñaptir upādāya pratipat saiva madhyamā // yo ’yaṃ pratītyasamutpādo hetupratyayān apekṣya aṅkuravijñānādīnāṃ prādurbhāvaḥ, sa svabhāvenānutpādaḥ. yaś ca svabhāvenānutpādo bhāvānāṃ sā śūnyatā.
nagarjuna-candrakirti/mulamadhyamakakari.english_close: What is dependent arising, that we declare to be emptiness. That is designation in dependence [on something]; that itself is the middle way. This dependent arising—the appearance of sprouts, cognitions and so forth depending upon causes and conditions—is nonarising by intrinsic nature. And the nonarising of things by intrinsic nature is emptiness.

nagarjuna-candrakirti/mulamadhyamakakari.notes: Root verses Nāgārjuna; prose Candrakīrti, with opponent/reply marked. The joined hetupratyayānapekṣya is resolved as hetupratyayān apekṣya (accusative plural + absolutive): “depending on causes and conditions.” This is word division, not a letter-level emendation. The e-text’s svabhāve nānutpādaḥ is corrected against printed स्वभावेनानुत्पादः = svabhāvena anutpādaḥ. Do not translate either junction as independence from conditions or intrinsic production.

salikanatha/prakarana-pancika/inspectabl.original_text: jāgrato hi meyāni mātā ca prakāśante. suṣuptasya tadā na tad dvayam api prakāśate. na ca tadānīṃ tad dvayam api nāsty eva, prabodhe pratyabhijñānāt. […] prakāśasya tv aprakāśamānasya sattaiva nābhyupeyate.
salikanatha/prakarana-pancika/inspectabl.english_close: For the waking person, objects known and the knower are manifest. For the deeply sleeping person, neither of those two is then manifest. Yet neither of them is simply nonexistent then, because they are recognized on awakening. […] But the existence of manifestation when it is not manifest is not accepted.

vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/inspectable-.english_close: From this it should be understood that, in sections concerning the individual self, the intention of scriptural declarations of unity of self is precisely discrimination, through nondifference characterized by absence of dissimilarity; for discriminative knowledge alone is said to cause liberation as correct knowledge. vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-wisdo.original_text: samādhiprajñāprabhavaḥ saṃskāro vyutthānasaṃskārāśayaṃ bādhate. vyutthānasaṃskārābhibhavāt tatprabhavāḥ pratyayā na bhavanti. […] katham asau saṃskārātiśayaś cittaṃ sādhikāraṃ na kariṣyatīti. na te prajñākṛtāḥ saṃskārāḥ kleśakṣayahetutvāc cittam adhikāraviśiṣṭaṃ kurvanti. cittaṃ hi te svakāryād avasādayanti. khyātiparyavasānaṃ hi cittaceṣṭitam iti.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-wisdo.english_close: The disposition arising from the wisdom of concentration counters the accumulated dispositions of emergence [from concentration]. Because the dispositions of emergence are overpowered, the cognitions produced by them do not occur. […] [Objection:] How will this increase of dispositions not give the mind an ongoing function? [Reply:] Those dispositions produced by wisdom do not endow the mind with an ongoing function, because they cause the exhaustion of afflictions. For they bring the mind to an end with respect to its own work: the activity of mind culminates in discernment.

vacaspati/tattva-vaisaradi/inspectable-y.english_close: [Objection:] Granted that dispassion, being a cognition, counters wisdom, which is cognitive; but how does it counter a disposition that is not a cognition? […] [Reply:] The meaning is that the wisdom-disposition is countered precisely by a disposition born of the higher dispassion cultivated for a long time, uninterruptedly and with care—not by cognition. […] And in the cessation of every modification there is no perception for the yogin, nor memory.

vacaspati/tattva-vaisaradi/inspectable-y.original_text: nanu dharmameghasya parā kāṣṭhā jñānaprasādamātraṃ paraṃ vairāgyaṃ samūlaghātam apahantu vyutthānasamādhisaṃskārān sakleśakarmāśayān guṇās tu svata eva vikārakaraṇaśīlāḥ kasmāt tādṛśam api puruṣaṃ prati dehendriyādīn nārabhanta ity ata āha. […] śīlam idaṃ guṇānāṃ yad amī yaṃ prati kṛtārthās taṃ prati na pravartanta iti bhāvaḥ.
vacaspati/tattva-vaisaradi/inspectable-y.english_close: [Objection:] Granted that the highest limit of the cloud of dharma—higher dispassion consisting solely of clarity of knowledge—destroys at their roots the dispositions of emergence and concentration and the deposits of affliction and karma; but the qualities by themselves are disposed to produce transformations. Why do they not initiate bodies, senses and so forth even for such a person? Therefore [the sūtra-author] says [4.32]. […] The meaning is: this is the disposition of the qualities, that they do not operate for the one for whom their purpose has been fulfilled.

The objection concerns this accomplished person, not universal cessation of the guṇas for every subject.

vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-chang.original_text: paramārthatas tv eka eva pariṇāmaḥ. dharmisvarūpamātro hi dharmo dharmivikriyaivaiṣā dharmadvārā prapañcyata iti. tatra dharmasya dharmiṇi vartamānasyaivādhvasv atītānāgatavartamāneṣu bhāvānyathātvaṃ bhavati na tu dravyānyathātvam. yathā suvarṇabhājanasya bhittvānyathākriyamāṇasya bhāvānyathātvaṃ bhavati na suvarṇānyathātvam iti.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-chang.english_close: But in truth there is just one transformation. For a property is nothing but the form of its bearer; this is precisely the bearer’s modification, elaborated through its properties. In this case, the property, while existing in its bearer, undergoes a change of condition across the past, future and present courses, but not a change of substance. Thus, when a gold vessel is broken and made otherwise, there is a change of condition, but no change of the gold.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-chang.notes: Received Vyāsa commentary, own exposition The following objection challenges persistence without immutable fixity; the author answers it. The fragment cannot alone establish the complete Yoga ontology or metaphysical nonduality.

vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-chang.original_text: tatredam udāharaṇaṃ mṛddharmī piṇḍākārād dharmād dharmāntaram upasaṃpadyamāno dharmataḥ pariṇamate ghaṭākāra iti. ghaṭākāro 'nāgataṃ lakṣaṇaṃ hitvā vartamānalakṣaṇaṃ pratipadyata iti lakṣaṇataḥ pariṇamate. ghaṭo navapurāṇatāṃ pratikṣaṇam anubhavann avasthāpariṇāmaṃ pratipadyata iti. dharmiṇo 'pi dharmāntaram avasthā dharmasyāpi lakṣaṇāntaram avasthety eka eva dravyapariṇāmo bhedenopadarśita iti. evaṃ padārthāntareṣv api yojyam iti.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-chang.english_close: Here is an example. The clay bearer, passing from the property of lump-form to another property, transforms with respect to property: it is pot-form. Pot-form leaves the future temporal mark and takes on the present temporal mark: it transforms with respect to temporal mark. The pot, undergoing newness and oldness at every moment, takes on transformation of condition. A further property is also a condition of the bearer, and a further temporal mark is a condition of the property. Thus one transformation of substance is displayed through distinctions. This is to be applied to other things as well.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-chang.notes: Received Vyāsa commentary, own exposition A coarse finite path can illustrate successive forms but does not encode the whole three-time account or moment-by-moment ageing.

vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-persi.original_text: yasya tu dharmamātram evedaṃ niranvayaṃ tasya bhogābhāvaḥ. kasmāt, anyena vijñānena kṛtasya karmaṇo 'nyat kathaṃ bhoktṛtvenādhikriyate. tatsmṛtyabhāvaś ca nānyadṛṣṭasya smaraṇam anyasyāstīti. vastupratyabhijñānāc ca sthito 'nvayī dharmī yo dharmānyathātvam abhyupagataḥ pratyabhijñāyate tasmān nedaṃ dharmamātraṃ niranvayam iti.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-persi.english_close: But for one for whom this is merely properties without a continuing connection, there is no experience [of the result]. Why? How can a different cognition be entitled as experiencer of an action done by another cognition? Nor would there be memory of it: one does not remember what another has seen. And because of recognition of an object, a persisting, continuing bearer is established: what has undergone alteration of property is recognized. Therefore this is not merely properties without a continuing connection.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-persi.notes: Received Vyāsa commentary, own exposition A functor recording an already-labelled bearer assumes the persistence at issue; it cannot by itself prove this argument against the alternative.

vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-two-p.original_text: dvayī ceyaṃ nityatā kūṭasthanityatā pariṇāminityatā ca. tatra kūṭasthanityatā puruṣasya. pariṇāminityatā guṇānām. yasmin pariṇamyamāne tattvaṃ na vihanyate tan nityam ubhayasya ca tattvānabhighātān nityatvam.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-two-p.english_close: And this permanence is twofold: immutable permanence and permanence through transformation. Of these, immutable permanence belongs to the conscious subject; permanence through transformation belongs to the guṇas. That is permanent whose reality is not destroyed while it transforms; both are permanent because the reality of each is undestroyed.

vijnanabhiksu/vijnanamrta-bhasya/inspect.original_text: nanu jīvabrahmaṇor bheda ukta iti kathaṃ jīvasya brahmāham iti jñānaṃ bhaved iti ced ucyate—yathā sāṃkhyamate ’ntaḥkaraṇād bhinno ’pi jīvas tasyātmatayā tasyāham iti pramāviṣayo bhavati, tathaiva jīvādidehāntebhyo bhinnam api brahma jīvādyātmatayāntaḥkaraṇasyāham iti pramāviṣayaḥ syāt. antaryāmitayā jīvādilayādhāratayā ca brahmaiva sarveṣāṃ pāramārthikātmety uktatvāt. yathā ca jīvātmatājñānād dehābhimānarūpāvidyānivṛttir bhavati tathaiva brahmātmatājñānāj jīvādyabhimānasya nivṛttiḥ syāt.
vijnanabhiksu/vijnanamrta-bhasya/inspect.english_close: Objection: Since difference between the individual and Brahman has been stated, how could the individual have the cognition “I am Brahman”? Reply: Just as, in the Sāṅkhya account, the individual, although different from the inner organ, is the object of that organ’s valid cognition “I” through being its self, so Brahman, although different from [things] beginning with the individual and ending with the body, could be the object of the inner organ’s valid cognition “I” through being the self of the individual and the rest. For it has been stated that Brahman alone is the ultimate self of all, through being the inner ruler and the support into which the individual and the rest dissolve. And just as ignorance in the form of identification with the body ceases through knowing the individual as self, so identification with the individual and the rest would cease through knowing Brahman as self.

vijnanabhiksu/vijnanamrta-bhasya/inspect.original_text: nanu viruddhau bhedābhedau katham ekatra saṃbhavata iti cet, anyonyābhāvalakṣaṇabhedasyāvibhāgalakṣaṇābhedenāvirodhāt. vibhāgāvibhāgarūpayor api bhedābhedayoḥ kālabhedena vyavahāraparamārthabhedena cāvirodhāc ca.
vijnanabhiksu/vijnanamrta-bhasya/inspect.english_close: Objection: How can difference and nondifference, being opposed, occur together in one [place]? [Reply:] Because difference characterized as mutual absence does not conflict with nondifference characterized as nondivision. And even difference and nondifference in the forms of division and nondivision do not conflict when time differs, and when practical and ultimate [standpoints] differ.

mathara/mathara-vrtti/inspectable-mathar.original_text: evam iti | yathā, etāni pañcaviṃśatitattvāni puruṣādyāni bhūtaparyantāni teṣām abhyāsas tattvābhyāsaḥ | abhyāsenaiva tattvadarśanam | tasmād abhyāsāt puruṣasya buddhir utpadyate | nāsmi tattvāni, na me tattvāni, nāhaṃ tattvānām, kiṃ tu prādhānikāny etāni | tasmāj jñānam utpadyata evamādi | apariśeṣaṃ niravaśeṣam ity arthaḥ | kiṃ cānyat (jñānaṃ yasmād āha) --- aviparyayāt | viparyayaḥ saṃśayas tadviparīto 'viparyayas tasmād aviparyayād asaṃśayād yathābhūtārthadarśanād viśuddham niravadyam avyāmiśraṃ kevalaṃ jñānam utpadyate prādurbhavati | kiṃ jñānam? guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhirūpam ity arthaḥ
mathara/mathara-vrtti/inspectable-mathar.english_close: As for “thus”: the practice of those twenty-five principles, beginning with the conscious subject and ending with the elements, is practice of the principles. It is precisely through practice that there is vision of the principles. From that practice cognition arises for the conscious subject: “I am not the principles; the principles are not mine; I do not belong to the principles. Rather, these belong to primordial nature.” Therefore knowledge arises, and so on. “Remainderless” means without remainder. What else? [The witness adds parenthetically: “knowledge, since he says”:] “from non-error.” Error is doubt; its opposite is non-error. From that non-error, from absence of doubt, from seeing the object as it actually is, pure—that is, faultless—unmixed, isolated knowledge arises, becomes manifest. What knowledge? [Knowledge] whose form is apprehending the difference between the guṇas and the conscious subject: this is the meaning.

vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-corre.original_text: yas tv ekāgre cetasi sadbhūtam arthaṃ pradyotayati kṣiṇoti ca kleśān karmabandhanāni ślathayati nirodham abhimukhaṃ karoti sa saṃprajñāto yoga ity ākhyāyate.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-corre.english_close: But the concentration which, in a one-pointed mind, illuminates an actually existing object, diminishes the afflictions, loosens the bonds of action and turns [the mind] toward cessation is called cognitive Yoga.

vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-doubl.original_text: mano hi mantavyenārthenoparaktaṃ, tat svayaṃ ca viṣayatvād viṣayiṇā puruṣeṇātmīyayā vṛttyābhisaṃbaddhaṃ, tad etac cittam eva draṣṭṛdṛśyoparaktaṃ viṣayaviṣayinirbhāsaṃ cetanācetanasvarūpāpannaṃ viṣayātmakam apy aviṣayātmakam ivācetanaṃ cetanam iva sphaṭikamaṇikalpaṃ sarvārtham ity ucyate.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-doubl.english_close: The mind is colored by the object to be thought. And since it is itself an object, it is connected with the conscious subject which has it as object, through a vṛtti belonging to that subject [the possessive is read here with Vācaspati’s explanation below]. This very mind, colored by seer and seen, presenting object and subject, having taken on the forms of conscious and unconscious, though of the nature of an object appearing as if not an object, and though unconscious appearing as if conscious, is called “having every object,” like a crystal jewel.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-doubl.notes: Received Vyāsa commentary, own exposition Base text and Vācaspati’s reading are distinguished. The exact account also differs from Bhikṣu’s reciprocal-reflection explanation; one cannot transfer the latter into this passage without argument.

vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-laten.original_text:
pratyayavivekanimnasya sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrapravāhiṇaś cittasya tacchidreṣu pratyayāntarāṇy asmīti vā mameti vā jānāmīti vā na jānāmīti vā. kutaḥ, kṣīyamāṇabījebhyaḥ pūrvasaṃskārebhya iti. 4.27
hānam eṣāṃ kleśavad uktam || ys_4.28 ||
 yathā kleśā dagdhabījabhāvā na prarohasamarthā bhavanti tathā jñānāgninā dagdhabījabhāvaḥ pūrvasaṃskāro na pratyayaprasūr bhavati.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-laten.english_close: In the gaps of the mind inclined toward discriminative cognition, whose flow is only the discernment of the distinction between sattva and the conscious subject, other cognitions occur: “I am,” “mine,” “I know,” or “I do not know.” From what? From previous dispositions whose seeds are diminishing. [Sūtra4.28:] Their removal has been explained as with the afflictions. Just as afflictions whose seeds have been burned cannot sprout, so a former disposition, its seed burned by the fire of knowledge, does not produce cognition.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-laten.voice: Vyāsa’s explanation of4.27 and4.28, with root4.28 explicitly included and distinguished in translation.
vyasa/yoga-bhasya/inspectable-yoga-laten.notes: Vyāsa’s explanation of4.27 and4.28, with root4.28 explicitly included and distinguished in translation. This is not a claim that all knowledge or all dispositions vanish at the first discriminative cognition. Following text treats knowledge-dispositions separately.

vacaspati/tattva-vaisaradi/inspectable-t.original_text: citeḥ svabuddhisaṃvedanaṃ buddhes tadākārāpattau citipratibimbādhāratayā tadrūpatāpattau satyām.
vacaspati/tattva-vaisaradi/inspectable-t.english_close: Consciousness apprehends its own intellect when the intellect takes on that form—when it takes on that form through being the support of the reflection of consciousness.
vacaspati/tattva-vaisaradi/inspectable-t.notes: Vācaspati’s commentary, own reply/explanation The opening problem asks how an inactive, unconnected subject could experience mind. This answer does not yet posit Bhikṣu’s second reflection of intellect in consciousness.

vacaspati/tattva-vaisaradi/inspectable-t.original_text: yathā hi candramasaḥ kriyām antareṇāpi saṃkrāntacandrapratibimbam amalaṃ jalam acalaṃ calam iva candramasam avabhāsayaty evaṃ vināpi citivyāpāram upasaṃkrāntacitipratibimbaṃ cittaṃ svagatayā kriyayā kriyāvatīm asaṅgatām api saṅgatāṃ citiśaktim avabhāsayad bhogyabhāvam āsādayad bhoktṛbhāvam āpādayati tasyā iti sūtrārthaḥ.
vacaspati/tattva-vaisaradi/inspectable-t.english_close: Just as clear water into which the moon’s reflection has entered makes the motionless moon appear as if moving, even without action by the moon, so the mind, into which the reflection of consciousness has entered, even without activity by consciousness, through its own activity makes consciousness-power appear active and connected although unconnected. In acquiring the condition of being experienced, it brings about for that [consciousness-power] the condition of being experiencer. This is the meaning of the sūtra.
vacaspati/tattva-vaisaradi/inspectable-t.notes: Vācaspati’s commentary, own reply/explanation Water here is clear, not expressly motionless; acalam qualifies the moon. No hidden assertion that an image is a second independently conscious subject.

vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/inspectable-.original_text: yathā ca citi buddheḥ pratibimbam evaṃ buddhāv api citpratibimbaṃ svīkāryam anyathā caitanyasya bhānānupapatteḥ svayaṃ sākṣāt svadarśane karmakartṛvirodhena buddhyārūḍhatayaivātmano ghaṭādivaj jñeyatvābhyupagamāt.
vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/inspectable-.english_close: And just as there is a reflection of intellect in consciousness, so a reflection of consciousness in intellect must also be accepted; otherwise the manifestation of consciousness would be inexplicable. vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/inspectable-.notes: Vijñānabhikṣu’s explanation and argument This is Bhikṣu’s solution. Do not attribute the same reasoning to all Advaitins, Trika, or every Yoga commentator.

vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/inspectable-.original_text: bimbākāro buddheḥ pariṇāma eva sa ca sākṣibhāsya iti. etena nīrūpatvād buddhipuruṣayor anyonyaṃ pratibimbanaṃ na sambhavatīty apāstam. ubhayatrobhayākārabuddhipariṇāmasyaiva pratibimbaśabdenātra vivakṣitatvāt.
vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/inspectable-.english_close: The form of the original is precisely a transformation of intellect, and that is manifested to the witness. By this, [the objection] that mutual reflection of intellect and person is impossible because of lack of form is set aside. For in both cases, precisely the transformation of intellect bearing the respective forms of the two is intended here by the word “reflection.”
vijnanabhiksu/yoga-varttika/inspectable-.notes: Vijñānabhikṣu’s explanation and argument This brief clause must be presented with the reciprocal argument, not as a freestanding account of every reflection.

shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-4.original_text: bahūni me mama vyatītāni atikrāntāni janmāni tava ca he arjuna tāny ahaṃ veda jāne sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha jānīṣe | dharmādharmādi-pratibaddha-jñāna-śaktitvāt | ahaṃ punar nitya-śuddha-buddha-mukta-svabhāvatvād anāvaraṇa-jñāna-śaktir iti vedāham | he parantapa
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-4.english_close: Many births of mine and of yours have passed, Arjuna. I know all of them; you do not know them, because your power of knowledge is obstructed by merit, demerit and the like. I, however, being of an eternally pure, awakened and free nature, have an unobstructed power of knowledge; therefore I know. O tormentor of foes.
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-4.notes: Śaṅkara’s own gloss No assertion that every saint has the Lord’s unrestricted knowledge follows.

shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-4.original_text: ajo 'pi janma-rahito 'pi san, tathāvyayātmākṣīṇa-jñāna-śakti-svabhāvo 'pi san, tathā bhūtānāṃ brahmādi-stamba-paryantānām īśvara īśana-śīlo 'pi san | prakṛtiṃ svāṃ mama vaiṣṇavīṃ māyāṃ triguṇātmikāṃ yasyā vaśe sarvam idaṃ jagad vartate | yayā mohitaṃ jagat sat svam ātmānaṃ vāsudevaṃ na jānāti | tāṃ prakṛtiṃ svām adhiṣṭhāya vaśīkṛtya saṃbhavāmi dehavān iva bhavāmi jāta ivātma-māyayātmano māyayā, na paramārthato lokavat
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-4.english_close: Although unborn, that is, free from birth; likewise although of imperishable self, whose nature is undiminished knowledge-power; likewise although Lord, disposed to ruling, of beings from Brahmā down to a clump of grass: [I take command of] my own prakṛti, my three-guṇa Vaiṣṇava māyā, under whose sway this entire world exists, deluded by which the world does not know Vāsudeva as its own self. Having taken command of that own prakṛti, having brought it under control, I come forth: I become as though embodied, as though born, through my own māyā—not ultimately as people do.
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-4.notes: Śaṅkara’s own gloss The as-if and not-ultimately clauses are explicit. The source does not say a finite ordinary body contains infinity as an ordinary spatial inclusion.

shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-4.original_text: taj-janma māyā-rūpaṃ, karma ca sādhu-paritrāṇādi, me mama divyam aprākṛtam aiśvaram evaṃ yathoktaṃ yo vetti tattvatas tattvena yathāvat tyaktvā deham imaṃ punar janma punar utpattiṃ naiti na prāpnoti, mām ety āgacchati, sa mucyate he 'rjuna
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-4.english_close: That birth has the form of māyā, and the action is protecting the good and the rest. Whoever knows this divine—nonordinary, lordly—birth and action of mine truly, just as stated, having abandoned this body, does not attain birth again; he comes to me, he is liberated, Arjuna.
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-4.notes: Śaṅkara’s own gloss Aprākṛta rendered nonordinary here; it must not be silently converted into another school’s technical theory of an eternal nonmaterial body.

shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-9.original_text: avajānanty avajñāṃ paribhavaṃ kurvanti māṃ mūḍhā avivekinaḥ | mānuṣīṃ manuṣyasaṃbandhinīṃ tanuṃ deham āśritam, manuṣyadehena vyavaharantamity etat, paraṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ bhāvaṃ param ātma-tattvam ākāśa-kalpam ākāśād apy antaratamam ajānanto mama bhūta-maheśvaraṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ mahāntam īśvaraṃ svātmānam | tataś ca tasya mamāvajñāna-bhāvanena āhatās te varākāḥ
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-9.english_close: The deluded, undiscriminating people disregard me: they show disrespect, contempt. “Having resorted to a human body” means transacting through a human body. They do not know my higher, excellent nature, the supreme reality of the self, like space, more inward even than space, the great Lord of beings, the great ruler of all beings, their own self. Therefore those pitiable people are injured by their attitude of disregard for me.
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-9.notes: Śaṅkara’s own gloss Space simile does not establish a physical space or a mathematical topology.

shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-d.original_text:
nanv anyāpi devatās tvam eva cet tad-bhaktāś ca tvām eva yajante | satyam evam -

ye 'py anya-devatā-bhaktā yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ |
te 'pi mām eva kaunteya yajanty avidhi-pūrvakam ||

ye 'py anya-devatā-bhaktā anyāsu devatāsu bhaktā anya-devatā-bhaktāḥ santo yajante pūjayanti śraddhayā āstikya-buddhyānvitā anugatāḥ, te 'pi mām eva kaunteya yajanty avidhi-pūrvakam avidhir ajñānaṃ tat-pūrvakaṃ yajanta ity arthaḥ

ahaṃ hi sarva-yajñānāṃ śrautānāṃ smārtānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yajñānāṃ devatātmatvena bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca | mat-svāmiko hi yajñaḥ, adhiyajño 'ham evātra [Gītā 8.4] iti hy uktam | tathā na tu mām abhijānanti tattvena yathāvat | ataś cāvidhi-pūrvakam iṣṭvā yāga-phalāc cyavanti pracyavante te
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-d.english_close: [Question:] If the other deities too are precisely you, their devotees also worship you. [Answer:] It is indeed so. [Root:] Even those devoted to other deities who worship endowed with faith worship precisely me, son of Kuntī, but preceded by a wrong procedure. [Śaṅkara:] Those devoted to other deities worship, honor, endowed with faith, an affirmative conviction. They too worship precisely me; avidhi is ignorance, and their worship is preceded by that—this is the meaning. For I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices, Vedic and remembered, as the self of the deities. A sacrifice indeed has me as its master; “I alone am the presiding deity of sacrifice here” was said. But they do not know me truly, as I am. Therefore, having sacrificed with ignorance preceding, they fall away from the fruit of sacrifice.
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-d.voice: Explicit question/affirmative reply, then root speaker, then Śaṅkara’s own glosses; separated blocks
shankara/gita-bhasya/inspectable-df-sh-d.notes: Explicit question/affirmative reply, then root speaker, then Śaṅkara’s own glosses; separated blocks Four explicitly separated blocks. Connected9.25 immediately says those worshippers do attain their appropriate sacrifice-fruit; fall away must not be read as no fruit whatever. Thus9.24/25 together prevent overstatement. Electronic intro anyāpi devatās retained as witness rather than silently regularized.

madhusudana/gudhartha-dipika/inspectable.english_close: Having taken my own nature as my basis, remaining precisely in my own nature, I come forth: without any body-and-body-possessor relation, I transact like an embodied one. How, then, is there an appearance of bodiliness in the bodiless mass of being-consciousness-bliss? To this he says, “through my own māyā.” In me, the Lord Vāsudeva, without guṇas, pure, a mass of being-consciousness-bliss, empty of the body-and-body-possessor relation, the appearance in that form is māyā alone—this is the meaning.

bhagavata/bhagavata-purana/inspectable-d.english_close: When the cowherd woman had thus known the truth, that mighty Lord extended Vaiṣṇava māyā consisting of affection for a son. Hari, whose greatness is sung by the threefold Veda, the Upaniṣads, Sāṅkhya and Yoga, and the Sātvatas, she regarded as her son.

jiva/bhagavat-sandarbha/inspectable-df-j.original_text: atraiva tāvat śrī-kṛṣṇākhye māyopaśamane’vatāre prādurbhāve, bahiś cāntar-jaṭhare ca sphuṭasya dṛṣṭasya kṛtsnasya jagataḥ sambandhe pūrvoktaṃ yan māyātvam, prapañca-kṛta-tvat-paricchedyatvasya mithyātvam | taj-jananyā jananyai te tvayā prakaṭīkṛtaṃ darśitam | tasmād bhavān jagad-antaḥstha eva, jagat tu bhavad-bahir-bhūtam ity evaṃ māyā-dharmaḥ | vastutas tu durvitarkya-svarūpa-śaktyā madhyamatve’pi vyāpako’sīti bhāvaḥ |
jiva/bhagavat-sandarbha/inspectable-df-j.english_close: Here itself, in the appearance called Śrī Kṛṣṇa that stills māyā, regarding the whole world clearly seen both outside and within the belly, the māyā-character mentioned before is the falsity of your being delimited by the manifold. That was disclosed—shown—by you to the mother. Thus, “You are only within the world, while the world is outside you”—such is a property of māyā. But in reality, through the intrinsic power difficult to reason out, you are pervasive even with middling size: this is the purport.
jiva/bhagavat-sandarbha/inspectable-df-j.voice: Jīva’s own explanation after quoting Brahmā’s BhP10.14.16. The preceding paragraph reports another interpretation with vyākurvanti; that alternative is not fused with this explanation.
jiva/bhagavat-sandarbha/inspectable-df-j.notes: Jīva’s own explanation after quoting Brahmā’s BhP10.14.16. The preceding paragraph reports another interpretation with vyākurvanti; that alternative is not fused with this explanation. Madhyamatva here contrasts a determinate perceptible magnitude with all-pervasiveness; it does not supply a numerical measurement. “Difficult to reason out” retains durvitarkya, without using it to authorize every arbitrary contradiction.

jiva/bhagavat-sandarbha/inspectable-df-j.original_text: svasya vraje’ntar-bhūtatā-darśanenaiva samaṃ vrajasya svasminn antar-bhūtatāṃ darśayan, tac cāntar-bahir-darśanaṃ kiṃ svapna etad uta deva-māyā [bhā.pu. 10.8.40] ity-ādau śrī-jananyā eva vicāre svāpnikatva-māyikatva-bimba-pratibimbatvānām ayogyatvād ekam evety abhijñāpayan, kiṃ svapna ity-ādāv eva, yaḥ kaścana autpattika ātma-yogaḥ [bhā.pu. 10.8.40] ity anena carama-pakṣāvasitayā durvitarkya-svarūpa-śaktyaiva madhyama-parimāṇa-viśeṣa eva sarva-vyāpako’smīti svayam eva bhagavān jananīṃ prati yugapad ubhayātmakaṃ nija-dharma-viśeṣaṃ darśitavān |
jiva/bhagavat-sandarbha/inspectable-df-j.english_close: Showing Vraja’s being within himself simultaneously with the display of his own being within Vraja, and making known that this inside-and-outside vision is one and the same—because dreamhood, illusionhood and original-and-reflection status are unsuitable in the mother’s own deliberation beginning “Is this a dream, or divine māyā?”—Bhagavān himself showed the mother his own particular property as having both characters simultaneously: “Precisely as a particular middling magnitude, I am all-pervading,” through the intrinsic power difficult to reason out, settled upon as the last alternative by “some innate power” in that same verse.
jiva/bhagavat-sandarbha/inspectable-df-j.voice: Jīva’s explanatory prose; the first-person “I am” is his formulation of what Bhagavān disclosed, not an additional quotation in the Bhāgavata root.
jiva/bhagavat-sandarbha/inspectable-df-j.notes: Jīva’s explanatory prose; the first-person “I am” is his formulation of what Bhagavān disclosed, not an additional quotation in the Bhāgavata root. This argument does not establish that every human or every god has this joint property. The clauses denying dream/illusion/reflection are Jīva’s interpretation of the episode;10.8.40 itself asks questions. An exact mathematical semantics has not yet been derived.

jiva/bhagavat-sandarbha/inspectable-df-j.english_close: That from which the forms of Vraja’s friends and the rest appeared, and by which all of that, at the time of disappearance, remains again as this divine form—that is precisely nondual Brahman: this is the meaning. The purport is that it falls under that characterization through the observed appearance, persistence and disappearance of all worldly and nonworldly things. Consequently, when its being Brahman is established, its pervasiveness too is established: this is the intention.

jayatirtha/prameyadipika/inspectable-df-.original_text: vibhūtimadādikaṃ mama tejorūpeṇāṃśena saha bhavatīty uktyā viṣṇvādīnām api bhagavadaṃśayuktatvaṃ pratīyate | teṣām apy etallakṣaṇopetatvāt | tannivṛttyartham āha—viṣṇvādīnīti || […] aṃśayuktatvenoktvā “kalāḥ” ity anena kalā iva kalāḥ | na svarūpatvena | “ete svāṃśakalāḥ” ity anena svarūpāṃśarūpā eva kalāḥ | natu pūrvavad upacāreṇeti ||
jayatirtha/prameyadipika/inspectable-df-.english_close: By saying that what possesses splendor and so forth exists together with my portion in the form of radiance, Viṣṇu and the others also appear to be endowed with a portion of Bhagavān, since they too have that characteristic. To remove this [understanding], he says “Viṣṇu and the others.” […] Having spoken of [the first group] as endowed with a portion, by “kalās”: they are kalās as if kalās, not as his own nature. By “these are own-portion kalās”: the kalās have precisely the character of portions of his own nature, not by figurative usage as before.

jayatirtha/prameyadipika/inspectable-df-.notes: Jayatīrtha explaining Madhva; quotation tokens retain the form given in this commentary witness. madhva-jayatirtha/anuvyakhyana-nyayasudh.original_text: sa cāprākṛtarūpatvād arūpaḥ svaguṇātmakam / rūpam asya śiraḥpāṇipādādyātmakam iṣyate // […] prakṛtiśabdo ’nyeṣāmapi tattvānāmupalakṣakaḥ / aprākṛtarūpatvāt / prākṛtarūparahitatvāt / guṇātmakamityukte sattvādīnāṃ pratītiḥ syāt / tannirāsārthaṃ svaśabdaḥ / ye paramātmanaḥ svarūpabhūtā guṇā ānandādyāstadātmakamiti / rūpaśabdena ca śuklādiguṇapratītiḥ syāt / ataḥ śiraḥpāṇīti vivaraṇaṃ kṛtam / ato rūpavāṃśceti śeṣaḥ / […] anityatā janmamaraṇavattā / nāpi saundaryādyabhāva iti ca draṣṭavyam / tathāca tasminbhaktirupapanneti śeṣaḥ /
madhva-jayatirtha/anuvyakhyana-nyayasudh.english_close: [Madhva:] And he is formless because his form is not prākṛta. His form, consisting of his own qualities and of head, hands, feet and the rest, is accepted. […] [Jayatīrtha:] The word prakṛti also indicates the other principles. “Because of having non-prākṛta form”: because of being devoid of a prākṛta form. If “consisting of qualities” were said [alone], sattva and the others might be understood; the word “own” removes that. It means consisting of the qualities that are the supreme Self’s own nature, bliss and the rest. And by “form,” the quality white and so forth might be understood; therefore “head, hands” supplies the explanation. Thus, “and he has form” is to be supplied. […] Impermanence is possession of birth and death. Nor is there absence of beauty and the rest: this too should be understood. Therefore devotion to him is coherent: this is to be supplied.

jayatirtha/nyaya-sudha/inspectable-df-m0.english_close: Whatever, even appearing as though contradictory, is established by a means of knowing in the Lord or elsewhere, and is not contrary to the Lord’s sovereignty—for example, simultaneity of smallness and greatness […]—all that is to be accepted as coherent through the Lord’s sovereignty, not rejected. But what is not established by a means of knowing must not be imagined, even if not contrary to that sovereignty, because imagining a hare’s horn and the like would follow.
jayatirtha/nyaya-sudha/inspectable-df-m0.voice: Jayatīrtha giving the boundary of an appeal to inconceivable power, after an extended objection/reply about the agency and awareness of divine-regulated manifestations.
jayatirtha/nyaya-sudha/inspectable-df-m0.notes: Jayatīrtha giving the boundary of an appeal to inconceivable power, after an extended objection/reply about the agency and awareness of divine-regulated manifestations. The omitted example concerns incomplete connected awareness in Arjuna and others, treated earlier in the same debate; its electronic word-junction is not silently emended. The source’s further claim that jīva–God unity undermines sovereignty is a school-internal argument, not a neutral proof against every retyped nondual proposal.

baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.original_text: aṃśa-śabditatve’pi paro matsyādir na evaṃ jīvavan na bhavati | tatra dṛṣṭāntam āha prakāśeti | yathā tejo’ṃśo raviḥ khadyotaś ca tejaḥ-śabditatve’pi naikarūpya-bhāk | yathā jalāṃśaḥ sudhā-madyādiś ca jala-śabditatve’pi na sāmyaṃ labhate, tadvat ||44||
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.english_close: Although called a portion, the supreme Matsya and the rest are not thus—not like the jīva. Here he gives the example “like light.” Just as the sun and a firefly, portions of radiance, do not have the same character despite both being called radiance; and just as nectar, liquor and the rest, portions of liquid, do not attain equality despite both being called liquid—so it is.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.voice: Baladeva’s own explanation of the sūtra, after raising whether Matsya-type portions differ from jīva-type portions.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.notes: Baladeva’s own explanation of the sūtra, after raising whether Matsya-type portions differ from jīva-type portions. The repeated negative na evaṃ…na bhavati is preserved, not silently streamlined. “Portions of radiance/liquid” follows the commentator’s illustrative language and is not a modern physical explanation.

baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.original_text: na te jīvavat tato bhidyante, tasyaiva vaidūryādivat tat-tad-bhāvāviṣkārāt | sarva-śakti-vyakty-avyakti-savyapekṣo hi tat-tad-vyapadeśaḥ | yaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛtsna-ṣāḍguṇya-vyañjako’ṃśī, sa evākṛtsna-tad-vyañjako dvy-eka-vyañjako vāṃśaḥ kalā cety ucyate | yathaikaḥ kṛtsna-ṣaṭ-śāstra-pravaktā sarvavid ucyate, sa eva kvacid akṛtsna-tad-vaktā dvy-eka-śāstra-vaktā ca sarvavit-kalpo’lpajñaś ceti |
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.english_close: They do not differ from him as the jīva does, because that very one reveals the respective forms, like a vaidūrya gem and the like. For the respective designation depends on the manifestation or nonmanifestation of all powers. That very Kṛṣṇa who, displaying all six divine excellences, is the possessor of portions, when not displaying all of them, or displaying two or one, is called a portion or a fraction. Just as one person who teaches all six disciplines is called all-knowing, that very person, somewhere teaching not all of them or teaching two or one, is called almost all-knowing or little-knowing.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.voice: Baladeva’s own explanatory reasoning, after an explicitly introduced smṛti quotation.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.notes: Baladeva’s own explanatory reasoning, after an explicitly introduced smṛti quotation. The six excellences and six teaching disciplines belong to the example’s traditional vocabulary. The paragraph does not by itself assign exact subsets to every avatāra. The source’s spelling savyapekṣa is retained.

baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.original_text: sarvātiśayi-prema-pūrṇa-parikaratva-druhiṇādi-vidvattama-vismāpaka-vaṃśa-mādhurya-sva-paryanta-sarva-vismāpaka-rūpa-mādhurya-niratiśaya-kāruṇyādayo yaśodā-stanandhaye kṛṣṇa eva nityāvirbhūtāḥ santi, na tu matsyāditve satīti tasyaiva tat-tad-bhāvāviṣkārān na matsyāder jīvavat tattvāntaratvaṃ, kintu tad-ātmakatvam eveti ||45||
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.english_close: Having associates filled with love surpassing all; the sweetness of the flute that astonishes even the most learned, Brahmā and others; the sweetness of form that astonishes everyone, up to himself; unsurpassed compassion and the rest—these are eternally manifest in Kṛṣṇa alone, the suckling of Yaśodā, not in the condition of Matsya and the rest. Thus, because that very one reveals those respective forms, Matsya and the rest are not another reality as a jīva is, but have precisely his nature.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.voice: Baladeva’s own conclusion; excerpt begins inside a longer enumeration whose preceding mention of powers and qualities supplies the grammatical subject.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.notes: Baladeva’s own conclusion; excerpt begins inside a longer enumeration whose preceding mention of powers and qualities supplies the grammatical subject. The Sanskrit is a long descriptive compound; hyphens are editorial aid. The excerpt’s grammatical dependence on the preceding sentence is explicit, not hidden. It does not say that Matsya lacks divine power or is a defective God.

baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.original_text: naivaṃ matsyādi-rūpasya, kintu deha-sambandha-rāhityaṃ sākṣāt pareśatvaṃ ca tasya śrūyate, ato mahān viśeṣaḥ | […] jīvasyāsantater apūrṇatvād avyatikaraḥ | pūrṇena matsyādinā sāmyaṃ nety arthaḥ | bālāgra-śata-bhāgasya [śve.u. 5.9] ity ādyā śrutir jīvasyāpūrtim āha | pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idam ity ādyā tu matsyādeḥ pūrtim ||47||
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.english_close: It is not so for the Matsya and other forms; rather, absence of association with a body and direct being-the-supreme-Lord are heard of it. Therefore there is a great distinction. […] There is no intermixture, because of the jīva’s nonextension, its incompleteness. The meaning is: there is no equality with complete Matsya and the rest. The revelation beginning “of the hundredth part of a hair-tip” declares the jīva’s incompleteness; that beginning “That is complete, this is complete” declares the completeness of Matsya and the rest.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.voice: Baladeva on two successive sūtras; explicit omission separates46 from47.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-df-g.notes: Baladeva on two successive sūtras; explicit omission separates46 from47. Asantati is glossed by the author as apūrṇatva here; do not infer a general spatial definition of every self from the English “nonextension.” The quotations of Upaniṣads are Baladeva’s cited forms, not new independent editions of those Upaniṣads.

ādyantarahitaṃ tattu na hastādyaṅgasaṃyutam /
na ca strīrūpamathavā na puṃrūpamathobhayam //
dīptyā pidhānaṃ netrāṇāṃ teṣāmāsīnmahīpate /

devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-same.english_close: But that was without beginning and end, not furnished with limbs such as hands; nor was it a female form, nor a male form, nor both. Through its brilliance their eyes were covered, O lord of the earth. And when the gods, again taking courage, looked, then that very same [luminosity] shone in a female form, divine and captivating.
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-same.notes: Vyāsa’s narration The syntax says the same luminosity appeared in female form. It does not establish physical identity of every finite body with this manifestation, nor say that the female shape itself has no spatial outline. End of31a is an explicit excerpt boundary;31b begins the accusative descriptive sequence completed at41.

pāśāṅkuśavarābhīticaturbāhuṃ trilocanām /
raktavastraparīdhānāṃ dāḍimīkusumaprabhām //
sarvaśṛṅgāraveṣāḍhyāṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtām /
sarvāśāpūrikāṃ sarvamātaraṃ sarvamohinīm //
prasādasumukhīmambāṃ mandasmitamukhāmbujām /
avyājakaruṇāmūrtiṃ dadṛśuḥ purataḥ surāḥ //
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-pers.english_close: The gods saw before them the three-eyed [Goddess], with four arms [bearing] noose, goad, boon and fearlessness, clothed in red, shining like a pomegranate flower; rich in every adornment of beauty, saluted by all the gods, fulfilling all hopes, mother of all, enchanting all; the Mother whose face was gracious, whose lotus-face bore a gentle smile, the embodiment of unfeigned compassion.
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-pers.notes: Vyāsa’s narration This is a narrated divine appearance to the gods; it does not by itself classify any named human saint as an avatāra. Boon/fearlessness are emblems or gestures in the four-arm description; the Sanskrit compresses these. The held IAST and PDF602 read sarvāśāpūrikāṃ; the Satsangdhara electronic text instead reads sarvāśāparipūrikāṃ. See variant register.

devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-powe.original_text:
iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā provāca parameśvarī /
mama śaktistu yā gaurī bhaviṣyati himālaye //
śivāya sā pradeyā syāt sā vaḥ kāryaṃ vidhāsyati /
bhaktiryaccaraṇāmbhoje bhūyādyuṣmākamādarāt //
himālayo hi manasā māmupāste 'tibhaktitaḥ /
tatastasya gṛhe janma mama priyakaraṃ matam //
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-powe.english_close: Having heard their words, the supreme Lady said: “My power who is Gaurī will come to be in Himālaya. She should be given to Śiva; she will accomplish your purpose. May your devotion to [her] lotus-feet arise with earnestness. For Himālaya worships me mentally with exceeding devotion. Therefore birth in his house is considered pleasing to me.”
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-powe.voice: Vyāsa’s speech introduction; then the Goddess herself
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-powe.notes: Vyāsa’s speech introduction; then the Goddess herself At64 yaccaraṇāmbhoje is literally at whose lotus-feet; the antecedent Gaurī is retained here. Satsangdhara’s Hindi paraphrase says my feet, while its Sanskrit preserves yac-. The held IAST places mama before priyakaram in65; the syntactic relation permits “birth in his house is pleasing to me” without silently changing to a possessive “my birth.” The first-person divine referent and Himālaya’s reply still supply the contextual birth identification.

devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-univ.original_text:
adya prapañce kīrtiḥ syājjaganmātā sutābhavat /
aho himālayasyāsya dhanyo 'sau bhāgyavāniti //
yasyāstu jaṭhare santi brahmāṇḍānāṃ ca koṭayaḥ /
saiva yasya sutā jātā ko vā syāttatsamo bhuvi //
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-univ.english_close: Today there would be this fame in the world: “The mother of the universe became a daughter! Ah, this Himālaya is fortunate, blessed!” But she in whose belly there are crores of cosmic eggs—she herself has become his daughter: who on earth could be his equal?
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-df-sakti-univ.notes: Himālaya’s response within Vyāsa’s narration This is anticipatory praise after a promise, not a report of a child’s mouth vision. Koṭi is crore/ten million; plural crores should not be silently translated as a mathematical infinity. This is not evidence for all traditions identifying all goddesses or saints identically.

vijnana-bhairava/vijnana-bhairava/inspec.original_text:
antaḥsvānubhavānandā vikalponmuktagocarā |
yāvasthā bharitākārā bhairavī bhairavātmanaḥ || 15 ||

tad vapus tattvato jñeyaṃ vimalaṃ viśvapūraṇam |
evaṃvidhe pare tattve kaḥ pūjyaḥ kaś ca tṛpyati || 16 ||

evaṃvidhā bhairavasya yāvasthā parigīyate |
sā parā pararūpeṇa parā devī prakīrtitā || 17 ||
vijnana-bhairava/vijnana-bhairava/inspec.english_close: That state of Bhairava’s self, Bhairavī, whose bliss is one’s own inward experience, whose domain is freed from conceptual construction, whose form is fullness—that is to be known as [his] body in truth, stainless, filling the universe. In such a supreme reality, who is to be worshipped and who is satisfied? That state of Bhairava which is celebrated in this manner—she is the Supreme; in the supreme manner [she] is proclaimed the supreme Goddess.
vijnana-bhairava/vijnana-bhairava/inspec.notes: Bhairava’s reply Do not turn vapus into a claim that every visible deity-image is already this state as delimited image. The question kaḥ pūjyaḥ is a qualification of the ultimate register, not a denial that the text supplies practices. This unit does not establish an avatāra taxonomy or identify human saints.

ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-df-rk.original_text: অবতার বা অবতারের অংশ, এদের বলে ঈশ্বরকোটি আর সাধারণ লোকদের বলে জীব বা জীবকোটি। যারা জীবকোটি তারা সাধনা করে ঈশ্বরলাভ করতে পারে; তারা সমাধিস্থ হয়ে আর ফেরে না।
ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-df-rk.english_close: An avatāra or a part of an avatāra—these are called īśvarakoṭi; ordinary people are called jīva or jīvakoṭi. Those who are jīvakoṭi can attain God through practice; having entered samādhi they do not return.

ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-df-rk.notes: Ramakrishna’s speech as recorded by M. (Mahendranath Gupta) Do not reword this as ordinary people cannot attain God: it says they can. Do not generalize the nonreturn claim to every tradition. The classification is M.’s report of Ramakrishna’s teaching, not an independently demonstrable classification of individuals.

তোমাকে ছুঁলে কি তোমার সব শরীরটা ছুঁতে হবে? যদি গঙ্গাস্নান করি তা হলে হরিদ্বার থেকে গঙ্গাসাগর পর্যন্ত কি ছুঁয়ে যেতে হবে?
[…]
‘আমি’ গেলে কি রইল তা কেউ জানতে পারে না, — মুখে বলতে পারে না। যা আছে তাই আছে! তখন খানিকটা এঁতে প্রকাশ হয়েছে আর বাদবাকিটা ওখানে প্রকাশ হয়েছে, — এ-সব মুখে বলা যায় না।
ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-df-rk.english_close: If I touch you, must I touch your whole body? If I bathe in the Ganges, must I then go on touching from Haridwar to Gangasagar? […] When the I goes, no one can know what remains—cannot say it in words. What is, is! Then, “a portion has manifested in this one and the remainder has manifested over there”—such things cannot be said in words.
ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-df-rk.voice: Ramakrishna’s speech as recorded by M. (Mahendranath Gupta)
ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-df-rk.notes: Ramakrishna’s speech as recorded by M. (Mahendranath Gupta) Analogy about access does not prove that every bodily part has all properties of the whole, nor that every saint possesses unlimited manifested power. Trailokya’s negative claim must not be quoted as Ramakrishna’s own conclusion. This excerpt omits the immediately preceding idiomatic “ananta ḍhukute cāo keno”; no disputed English rendering of that phrase is used as a premise. The ellipsis omits the intervening maxim and sentence that difference-consciousness lasts while the I remains; it changes neither speaker nor argument. The retained no-one-can-know wording should not be converted into a separate doctrine of annihilation or ignorance in liberation.

ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-df-rk.english_close: The I of avatāras and the like is a thin I. Through this I, God can always be seen. […] This means that even though they assume a body, they always remain in yoga! […] Even after entering samādhi, they can come down again.

ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-df-rk.notes: Ramakrishna’s speech as recorded by M. (Mahendranath Gupta) The passage concerns avatāras and the like, called īśvarakoṭi nearby; it does not make all ordinary personalities or every liberated person equally transparent. The first ellipsis omits the wall/aperture illustration; the second omits its explanation of entering samādhi at will and going and coming through the large aperture. The embodied-yoga and return clauses are included.
