madhusudana/advaitasiddhi/inspectable-na.original_text: nanv evaṃ sati yāvatsadadhikaraṇātyantābhāvapratiyogitvaṃ paryavasitam. tathā ca kevalānvayyatyantābhāvapratiyogiṣu avṛttiṣu gaganādiṣu tārkikāṇāṃ siddhasādhanam; yadadhikaraṇaṃ yat sat tanniṣṭhātyantābhāvapratiyogitvaṃ tasya mithyātvam iti vivakṣāyām, adhikaraṇapadenāvṛttinirākaraṇe ’pi saṃyogasambandhena samavāyasambandhena vā yat ghaṭādhikaraṇaṃ samavāyasambandhena saṃyogasambandhena vā ghaṭasya tanniṣṭhātyantābhāvapratiyogitayā sarveṣu vṛttimatsu duruddharaṃ siddhasādhanam. yena sambandhena yad yasyādhikaraṇaṃ tena sambandhena tanniṣṭhātyantābhāvapratiyogitvam iti vivakṣāyām avyāpyavṛttiṣu saṃyogādiṣu siddhasādhanam iti cen na.
madhusudana/advaitasiddhi/inspectable-na.english_close: But, if this is so, [the definition] comes to being the counterpositive of absolute absence whose loci are all existent things. Then, for the logicians, in the case of things such as space which do not occur [in a locus] and are counterpositives of an absolute absence occurring universally, it proves what is already established. If what is intended is “its falsity is being the counterpositive of absolute absence located in that existent thing which is its locus,” then, even though the word “locus” excludes things that do not occur [in a locus], proving what is already established is hard to avoid for all things that do occur [in a locus]: where something is the locus of a pot through contact or inherence, the pot is the counterpositive of absolute absence there through inherence or contact [respectively]. If what is intended is being the counterpositive of absolute absence located there through the very relation through which something is its locus, there is [still] proving what is already established in cases such as contact, which does not occur throughout its locus. If this is the objection: no.
madhusudana/advaitasiddhi/inspectable-na.voice: Author reports an opponent’s successive objections; closes with his rejection, iti cen na.
madhusudana/advaitasiddhi/inspectable-na.notes: Author reports an opponent’s successive objections; closes with his rejection, iti cen na. Kevalānvayin and avṛtti describe the logicians’ accepted cases in this objection. Do not attribute their whole ontology to Madhusūdana or interpret siddhasādhana as a proof that he accepts ordinary pots as ultimately real.

madhusudana/advaitasiddhi/inspectable-na.original_text: yadi punaḥ dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvapratiyogitvam ivātyantābhāvapratiyogitvam ākāśādau na syāt; sādhakamānābhāvasya tulyatvāt, ihākāśo nāstīti pratyakṣapratītyasambhavāt, anumāne cānukūlatarkābhāvāt, sāmānyato dṛṣṭamātreṇa dhvaṃsaprāgabhāvapratiyogitvasyāpi siddhiprasaṅgāt, tadvyatirekeṇa kasyacit kāryasyānupapatter abhāvāc ca, evaṃ saṃyogasambandhena ghaṭavati bhūtale samavāyasambandhena ghaṭābhāvasattve mānābhāvāl lāghavena ghaṭātyantābhāvatvenaiva ghaṭasāmānādhikaraṇyavirodhitvakalpanāt sambandhaviśeṣapraveśe ca gauravāt ghaṭasamavāyamātraviṣayatayā pratīter upapatter ādhārādheyabhāvasya pratyakṣasiddhatvena ghaṭasyāvṛttitvaśaṅkānudayād uktayukteś ca na ghaṭāder atyantābhāvasāmānādhikaraṇyam; evaṃ ca saṃyogatadabhāvayor naikādhikaraṇyam; agre vṛkṣaḥ kapisaṃyogī mūle neti pratīter agramūlayor eva saṃyogatadabhāvavattayopapatteḥ, tadā sanmātraniṣṭhātyantābhāvapratiyogitvam eva mithyātvaṃ mantavyam.
madhusudana/advaitasiddhi/inspectable-na.english_close: If, however, space and the like were not counterpositives of absolute absence, just as they are not counterpositives of destruction or prior absence—because the lack of establishing evidence is the same; because direct apprehension “space is not here” is impossible; because inference lacks a supporting suppositional argument; because mere inference from general observation would also establish their being counterpositives of destruction and prior absence; and because no effect would be inexplicable without it—and likewise a pot and the like do not share a locus with [their] absolute absence, because there is no evidence for a pot’s absence through inherence on ground that has a pot through contact; because economy warrants positing incompatibility with sharing a locus with a pot simply through being absolute absence of a pot; because introducing a particular relation adds complexity; because the apprehension is explicable as having only the pot’s inherence as its object; because the directly established relation of support and supported prevents a doubt that the pot occurs nowhere; and because of the reasoning already stated; and likewise contact and its absence do not have one locus, since the apprehension “the tree has contact with a monkey at its top, not at its root” is explicable by the top and root themselves having contact and its absence—then falsity is to be understood simply as being the counterpositive of absolute absence located in existent reality as such.
madhusudana/advaitasiddhi/inspectable-na.voice: Author’s conditional alternative: yadi punaḥ ... tadā ... mantavyam.
madhusudana/advaitasiddhi/inspectable-na.notes: Author’s conditional alternative: yadi punaḥ ... tadā ... mantavyam. Sanmātra is translated cautiously as existent reality as such; it is not the finite set of ordinary objects by stipulation. This passage does not establish a topos, a universal consistency theorem, or the equivalence of every school.

annambhatta/tarka-samgraha/inspectable-n.original_text: anādiḥ sāntaḥ prāgabhāvaḥ. utpatteḥ pūrvaṃ kāryasya. sādir anantaḥ pradhvaṃsaḥ. utpattyanantaraṃ kāryasya. traikālikasaṃsargāvacchinnapratiyogitāko ’tyantābhāvaḥ. yathā bhūtale ghaṭo nāstīti. tādātmyasambandhāvacchinnapratiyogitāko ’nyonyābhāvaḥ. yathā ghaṭaḥ paṭo na bhavatīti.
annambhatta/tarka-samgraha/inspectable-n.english_close: Prior absence is beginningless and has an end: [the absence] of an effect before its production. Destruction has a beginning and no end: [the absence] of an effect after its production. Absolute absence has counterpositiveness delimited by a relation and holds through all three times; for example, “There is no pot on the ground.” Mutual absence has counterpositiveness delimited by the relation of identity; for example, “A pot is not a cloth.”
annambhatta/tarka-samgraha/inspectable-n.notes: Annambhaṭṭa root text The text here does not establish that every act of negation belongs to a modern Boolean algebra. The GRETIL compilation duplicates the root with divergent wording; this quote follows the inspected1930print rather than combining variants. The nextunit exposes the Dīpikā explanation used in translation.

annambhatta/tarka-samgraha-dipika/inspec.english_close: He defines absolute absence with “of all three times.” “Delimited by a relation” is to prevent overextension to mutual absence. “Of all three times” is to prevent overextension to destruction and prior absence.

annambhatta/tarka-samgraha-dipika/inspec.english_close: In that which has a pot through the relation of contact, there is absence of the pot through the relation of inherence. And the generic absence whose counterpositive is delimited by pothood is additional to the absences of this and that pot.
annambhatta/tarka-samgraha-dipika/inspec.notes: Annambhaṭṭa’s own commentary The preceding Devadatta/staff example and compressed introductory compound have documented manuscript/editorial difficulties in this edition; they are not used as unqualified quotation here. The selected contact/inherence and specific/generic examples are legible and correspond to the GRETIL reading, apart from explicit sambandha wording. No claim of a critical edition has been made. The inspected print reads pratiyogika, whereas the held GRETIL transcription reads pratiyogitāka; the quotation and translation here follow the print. This small variant does not change the distinction between particular and generic absence.

abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/insp.original_text: na bhavanti ca dharādīny uttarottaratattvāni jalādi pūrvapūrvaṃ vineti tāvatsvarūpāṇy eva / dharā hi na jalaṃ vinā bhavet sruter eva kāṭhinye darśanād ity evaṃkrameṇa bhūtāni tanmātrair vinā katham, tāny api indriyajṛmbhayā vinā, indriyāṇy api tattathāvidhādhyavasāyena vinā / sarvāṇi caitadādyāvibhaktānvitasūkṣmarūpamūlakāraṇavinākṛtāni na bhavanti / mūlaprakṛtir api bhogyā bhoktāraṃ tadbhogyavibhāgabhāgitvād eva saṃkucitaṃ saṃkocavaśād eva ca svātmārohitakālakalādipāśajālaṃ saṃvidātmakaṃ cāntareṇa kathaṃ / saṃvidaś cākhaṇḍarūpāyāḥ kathaṃ saṃkocakāraṇasvātantryaṃ māyāparaparyāyaṃ vinā saṃkucitatvam
abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/insp.english_close: Earth and the other successively later principles do not exist without the successively earlier water and so on; therefore they have that much as their nature. For earth would not exist without water, since what flows itself is seen in hardness. Thus, in this order: how [could] the elements [exist] without the subtle elements, those without the unfolding of the senses, and the senses without determination of that particular kind? And all these do not exist deprived of the root cause whose subtle form is connected with them undividedly at their beginning. And how [could] root nature, which is to be experienced, [exist] without an experiencer whose nature is awareness, contracted precisely through sharing in that division of objects of experience, and, through contraction itself, bearing upon itself the net of bonds beginning with time and limited agency? And how [could] undivided awareness have contraction without freedom, the cause of contraction, also designated māyā?
abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/insp.notes: authorial teaching This is Abhinavagupta’s argument, not independently established physics. The next compressed compound concerning degrees of contraction is not translated here; the separately quoted final sentence gives the Bhairava conclusion. No full thirty-six-item taxonomy is supplied.

jiva/priti-sandarbha/inspectable-pl-g14-.english_close: First, it is not, as [on the view] of the Sāṅkhyas, in the form of māyā-made bliss consisting of material sattva, because scripture declares that the Lord cannot be overcome by māyā, and because He is satisfied in Himself. Nor is it, as [on the view] of the advocates of the undifferentiated, in the form of the bliss of the Lord’s intrinsic nature, because an intensification would be inexplicable. Still less, therefore, is it in the form of the individual self’s intrinsic bliss, because that is exceedingly small.

jayatirtha/nyaya-sudha/inspectable-pl-md.english_close: Moreover, in the first two examples there is at least a cause–effect relation, but the words “one” and so forth would still be pointless. This, however, does not fit at all: “Just as, dear one, through one nail-cutter.” For, because the nail-cutter is a final composite, its being a cause of another iron object is itself impossible. How much less could one [be the cause] of all? Thus [Madhva] says “and not.”
jayatirtha/nyaya-sudha/inspectable-pl-md.voice: Jayatīrtha’s own challenge to the rival interpretation, introducing Madhva’s following verse; the Upaniṣad phrase is his cited wording.
jayatirtha/nyaya-sudha/inspectable-pl-md.notes: Jayatīrtha’s own challenge to the rival interpretation, introducing Madhva’s following verse; the Upaniṣad phrase is his cited wording. Antyāvayavin is rendered final composite, preserving the premise that this specimen is a completed implement rather than the material out of which every iron object is made. The final na ca introduces Madhva’s next root line; the translation does not treat it as an unexplained new conclusion.

jayatirtha/nyaya-sudha/inspectable-pl-md.english_close: Here, by “even ignorant of ordinary [names],” it is indicated that this is relative to results. If [one objects], “Then knowing all through knowing one would be nonprimary”—true. For even the opponent cannot explain it in the primary sense. If that were so, it would follow that a person who had seen clay would have no desire to know particular configurations such as pots and dishes, and the rest.

baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-pl-g.english_close: That [promise] can indeed obtain if the taught [reality] is the material cause, because the effect is nonseparate from it. But its nonseparateness from an efficient cause does not [obtain], because potter and pot are separate. […] And that [knowledge of the effect through knowledge of its material cause] could not obtain if merely efficient causation were accepted. For, when the potter is known, the pot is not [thereby] known.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-pl-g.voice: Baladeva’s own reply; sā refers to the one-known/all-known promise. The omitted sentence quotes the clay example and explains knowledge of the effect through knowledge of its material cause, supplying the second demonstrative’s antecedent.
baladeva/govinda-bhasya/inspectable-pl-g.notes: Baladeva’s own reply; sā refers to the one-known/all-known promise. The omitted sentence quotes the clay example and explains knowledge of the effect through knowledge of its material cause, supplying the second demonstrative’s antecedent. The ellipsis omits the cited Chāndogya clay sentence, not an objection or a change of speaker. This is the source’s causal argument; it does not make all generic dependence material nonseparation.

vallabha/anu-bhasya/inspectable-pl-v12-s.original_text: yathā prāṇāpānānāṃ niyamane jīvanamātram | aniyamane ākuñcanādi naitāvatā prāṇabhedaḥ pūrvam asattvaṃ vā | tathā jagato’pi | jñānakriyābhedāt sūtradvayam |
vallabha/anu-bhasya/inspectable-pl-v12-s.english_close: Just as, when prāṇa, apāna and the other [vital breaths] are restrained, there is only maintenance of life; when not restrained, contraction and so forth. utpaladeva/isvara-pratyabhijna-vrtti/ins.original_text: etādṛśaśuddhasvātantryavaśān naiṣa pṛthag eva labdhapratiṣṭhaṃ vastv avaiti, api tv ajñeyam ātmānam aniyantritaprabhāvatayā jñeyīkaroti / bhinnajñeyasāpekṣatve jñānakartṛtā mlāyet
utpaladeva/isvara-pratyabhijna-vrtti/ins.english_close: Through such pure independence, this [subject] does not know an entity established separately; rather, through unrestricted power, it makes its own self, which is not an object of knowledge, an object of knowledge. ksemaraja/pratyabhijna-hrdayam/inspectab.original_text: viśvasya sadāśivādeḥ bhūmyantasya siddhau niṣpattau prakāśane sthityātmani parapramātṛviśrāntyātmani ca saṃhāre parāśaktirūpā citir eva bhagavatī svatantrā anuttaravimarśamayī śivabhaṭṭārakābhinnā hetuḥ kāraṇam
ksemaraja/pratyabhijna-hrdayam/inspectab.english_close: In the establishment of the universe, from Sadāśiva to earth—in production, in manifestation consisting in continuance, and in withdrawal consisting in repose in the supreme knower—the cause is the Goddess consciousness alone: independent, consisting of unsurpassed reflexive apprehension, having the form of supreme power, nondifferent from Lord Śiva.

abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/insp.original_text: tatpurvo 'pi bhāgas taduttarabhāgapṛṣṭhapātivṛttapūrvaparipūrṇabhāsāsāravimarśatādātmyāt taduttararūpaparipūrṇatām ajahat svayaṃ ca svarūpanāntarīyakatāhaṭhakṛṣṭasvapūrvapūrvatarādibhāgāntarābhogo bhāsamāno vimṛśyamānaś ca tathaivākhaṇḍita
abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/insp.english_close: The preceding portion too, because of its identity with reflexive apprehension whose essence is the complete illumination that previously occurred upon the subsequent portion, does not abandon the completeness of that subsequent form; itself also encompassing the other portions prior and still prior to itself, forcibly drawn in by their necessary connection with its intrinsic nature, it is illuminated and reflexively apprehended, likewise undivided.
abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/insp.notes: Abhinavagupta The excerpt stops before iti. “Previously occurred” is crucial: retention is not inferred from bare causal dependence.

abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/insp.original_text: tad evaṃ prathamaṃ tāvad dharā tato 'pi jalaṃ tathaiva svarūpasākalyena bhāsamānaṃ vimṛśyamānaṃ ca tadbhāsāvimarśacamatkāram antaḥkṛtatathāvidhadharaṇitattvasaṃskārasattākaṃ pūrayed eveti yāvad ante saiva pūrṇasaṃvidbhagavatī śivātmaiva
abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/insp.english_close: Thus, first earth, then water, likewise being illuminated and reflexively apprehended in the entirety of its intrinsic nature, would fill out the savoring of that illumination and reflexive apprehension, which contains within it the existing impression of earth-principle of that kind—until, at the end, that very complete Goddess awareness has precisely Śiva as her nature.
abhinavagupta/paratrimsika-vivarana/insp.notes: Abhinavagupta The earth-impression is of the previously specified complete apprehension; this is not a claim about every ordinary memory.

apratarkyam anirdeśyamanaupamyamanāmayam /
tasya kācitsvataḥ siddhā śaktirmāyeti viśrutā // 2.3 //
na satī sā nāsatī sā nobhayātmā virodhataḥ /

anavasthādoṣasattvānna svenāpi prakāśitam /
karmakartrīvirodhaḥ syāttasmāttaddīpavatsvayam // 2.13 //
prakāśamānamanyeṣāṃ bhāsakaṃ viddhi parvata /
ata eva ca nityatvaṃ siddhasaṃvittanormama // 2.14 //
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-sakti-context.english_close: Because there would be the fault of infinite regress, [consciousness is not illuminated by another]; nor is it illuminated by itself, for a contradiction between object and agent would follow. Therefore know it, like a lamp, as shining of itself and illuminating others, O mountain. For that very reason the eternity of me, whose body is established awareness, [is established].
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-sakti-context.notes: Devīgītā, Goddess as speaker The bracketed clause carries forward 2.12. The sentence about the lamp continues across the verse boundary; it is not cut at 2.13.

devi/devi-gita/inspectable-sakti-context.original_text:
jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyādau dṛśyasya vyabhicārataḥ /
saṃvido vyabhicāraśca nānubhūto 'sti karhicit // 2.15 //
yadi tasyāpyanubhavastarhyayaṃ yena sākṣiṇā /
anubhūtaḥ sa evātra śiṣṭaḥ saṃvidvapuḥ purā // 2.16 //
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-sakti-context.english_close: Because the seen varies in waking, dream, deep sleep and the other [states], whereas variation of awareness has never been experienced. If that too were experienced, then the witness by which this was experienced is itself what remains here, having awareness as its body, as before.
devi/devi-gita/inspectable-sakti-context.notes: Devīgītā, Goddess as speaker The initial because continues the preceding eternity argument; tasyāḥ refers to awareness.

jñānasya jaḍaśeṣatvaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ na ca saṃbhavi /
ciddharmatvaṃ tathā nāsti citaścinna hi bhidyate // 2.20 //

devi/devi-gita/inspectable-sakti-context.english_close: Knowledge’s subordination to the inert is neither seen nor possible. Nor can it be a property of consciousness, for consciousness does not differ from consciousness. Therefore the self always has the form of knowledge and happiness, is real, full and unattached, devoid of the net of duality.

natanananda/cidvalli/inspectable-sakti-c.original_text:
अत्र
शिवशब्देन ज्ञानशक्तिरभिधीयते ज्ञानशक्त्यधिष्ठानत्वात् शिवतत्त्वस्य
शक्तिशब्देनापि क्रियाशक्तिरभिधीयते क्रियाशक्त्यधिष्ठानत्वात् शक्तितत्त्वस्य
चिदानन्दस्वरूपिण्याः सर्वत्र ज्ञानक्रियाभ्यामेव निर्माणौचित्यदर्शनात्
natanananda/cidvalli/inspectable-sakti-c.english_close: Here the word Śiva denotes the power of knowledge, because the Śiva-principle is the seat of the power of knowledge. The word Śakti too denotes the power of action, because the Śakti-principle is the seat of the power of action; for, in the case of her whose nature is consciousness and bliss, the fittingness of construction everywhere through knowledge and action alone is seen.

ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-sakti.original_text: ঈশ্বরকোটির আলাদা কথা, — যেমন অনুলোম বোলুম। ‘নেতি’ ‘নেতি’ করে ছাদে পৌঁছে যখন দেখে, ছাদও যে জিনিসে তৈরী, — ইঁট, চুন, সুরকি, সিঁড়িও সেই জিনিসে তৈরী। তখন কখন ছাদেও থাকতে পারে, আবার উঠা নামাও করতে পারে।
ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-sakti.english_close: The īśvarakoṭi is a different matter—like going in order and in reverse. Having reached the roof by “not this, not this,” when one sees that the stairs too are made of the same material as the roof—brick, lime and brick-dust—then one may sometimes remain on the roof, and may also go up and down.
ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-sakti.notes: Ramakrishna as recorded by M. The held Bengali has the colloquial anuloṃ boloṃ wording অনুলোম বোলুম; it is not silently replaced by a Sanskrit compound.
ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-sakti.translation_provenance: Site literal translation of the selected source wording.
ramakrishna/kathamrita/inspectable-sakti.romanized_text: Īśvarakoṭir ālādā kathā, — yeman anulom bolum. “Neti” “neti” kare chāde pãuche yakhan dekhe, chādao ye jinise tairī, — ĩṭ, cun, surki, sĩṛio sei jinise tairī. Takhan kakhana chādeo thākte pāre, ābār uṭhā nāmāo karte pāre.

vivekananda/complete-works/inspectable-s.original_text: The next question is to know what comes after realisation. aurobindo/life-divine/inspectable-sakti-.original_text: But the contradiction disappears when we understand that the indeterminability is not in its true sense negative, not an imposition of incapacity on the Inﬁnite, but positive, a freedom within itself from limitation by its own determinations and necessarily a freedom from all external determination by anything not itself, since there is no real possibility of such a not-self coming into existence.

aurobindo/life-divine/inspectable-sakti-.original_text: In fact the Inﬁnite does not create, it manifests what is in itself, in its own essence of reality; it is itself that essence of all reality and all realities are powers of that one Reality. aurobindo/life-divine/inspectable-sakti-.original_text: The opposition we make is mental and conceptual; in reality, the silence of the Spirit and the dynamis of the Spirit are complementary truths and inseparable. The immutable silent Spirit may hold its inﬁnite energy silent and immobile within it, for it is not bound by its own forces, is not their subject or instrument, but it does possess them, does release them, is capable of an eternal and inﬁnite action, does not weary or need to stop, and yet all the time its silent immobility inherent in its action and movement is not for a moment shaken or disturbed or altered by its action and movement;

aurobindo/life-divine/inspectable-sakti-.original_text: And since consciousness is the nature of the original Existence and the essence of its Force, this truth must be a self-perception in Conscious-Being and this determination of the line taken by Force must result from a power of selfdirective knowledge inherent in Consciousness which enables it to guide its own Force inevitably along the logical line of the original self-perception. medhananda/infinite-paths-to-infinite-re.original_text: Like fire and its power to burn, Brahman and Śakti mutually entail each other. The bidirectionality of all these analogies clearly rules out an Advaitic interpretation of Sri Ramakrishna’s doctrine of the inseparability of Brahman and Śakti. According to Advaita, Śakti is ontologically dependent on nirguṇa Brahman, but nirguṇa Brahman is not ontologically dependent on Śakti, since Śakti is ultimately unreal. Sri Ramakrishna, by contrast, teaches the mutual ontological dependence of Brahman and Śakti.

prakasatman/pancapadika-vivarana/reader-.english_close: [Objection:] If [one says], “Then, because resting on intrinsic nature is untenable, resting on the qualified [subject] is posited”—[reply:] no; because the connection with intrinsic nature exists even in the qualified [subject], and because, if the inert [inner organ] were the locus of ignorance, erroneous and correct cognition too would have to have that as their locus. [Objection:] But the difficulty is equal even in Brahman, the intrinsic nature. [Reply:] True. Rather than positing [ignorance’s] resting on two untenable [supports], it is preferable to adopt its resting on the acknowledged intrinsic nature.
